Title: Houthis claim Saudi strikes killed 33 in Yemen, including 13 children
Article:
SANAA: Houthi authorities said on Sunday that Saudi strikes killed 33 people, many of them women and children, in Yemen's Sanaa province, as deaths mount in the country's revived civil war.
The United Nations says more than 1,600 people have been killed and more than 300,000 displaced since fighting resumed in the impoverished country.
The death toll from the Saudi-led coalition's strikes on Al-Shariya village located east of Yemen's capital Sanaa has risen to 33, with 39 people wounded, Houthi health ministry spokesman Anees Alasbahi said in a post on X.
The Houthis' Saba news agency said on Saturday that operations to recover victims from the rubble were ongoing and that "aircraft targeted paramedics with two strikes."
"According to the near-final figures, the dead include 12 men, 8 women and 13 children, while the injured include 16 men, 10 women and 13 children," Alasbahi said.
The Iran-backed group's Al-Masirah TV broadcast footage that it said was filmed in Al-Shariya, showing smoke rising from a struck site, piles of debris and wounded people in hospital.
Saudi Arabia, fighting in Yemen in support of the internationally recognised government, has not commented on the report.
The Saudi-led coalition in a statement on Saturday said it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi missile launched towards Riyadh province.
The Houthis, meanwhile, said they had launched multiple missile and drone attacks against Saudi troops and infrastructure both in the Gulf kingdom and Yemen.
The group said six operations targeted Aramco oil facilities, Riyadh airport and Saudi military positions on both sides of the border, Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree posted on X.
On Friday, an attack on a market in Taiz province killed 30 people. The Houthis said Saudi airstrikes were to blame, while Yemen's government forces accused the Iran-backed group of having fired a ballistic missile at the site.
Yemen slipped back into war between the Houthis and the Saudi-backed government in July after years of relative calm, opening a new front in the conflict in the Middle East.
Since then, Saudi Arabia has regularly bombed Houthi positions, while the group has multiplied its attacks against the oil-rich kingdom.--AFP

Title: Qiulae Wong, the outsider who could decide New Zealand's next government
Article:
QIULAE Wong has been a politician for less than a year, but the 38-year-old could hold the balance of power in New Zealand's parliament after initial counting in Saturday's general election ended without a clear victor.
Prime Minister Christopher Luxon's centre-right coalition could govern with a majority of just two seats, Electoral Commission preliminary results showed, but that slim margin could disappear once special votes, which typically favour the left, are released at the official count on Nov 27.
That would mean either a centre-right or centre-left bloc would require the support of Wong's centrist Opportunity Party, which looks likely to enter parliament for the first time.
Either Luxon's National party or Labour, led by Chris Hipkins, are expected to try to form a coalition government in the coming days or weeks.
Wong, a former sustainable-business consultant, answered a job advertisement to head the decade-old party, taking over in November 2025.
She quickly oversaw a rebrand and dramatic rise in Opportunity's popularity, and its current vote share of 5.96 per cent would give it seven seats in a 131-member parliament, Electoral Commission data showed.
"It might seem like we've just arrived, that this is an overnight success, but to many in this room, this result has been a long time coming," Wong told cheering supporters in Auckland on Saturday night.
Opportunity's flagship policies centre on tax, with an annual NZ$19,400 (US$10,800) universal basic income for most New Zealand residents funded by a 1.75 per cent annual land tax.
The party also wants to simplify the country's income tax system.
"There's also been a shift globally around seeing the need to tax work less and tax wealth more or tax assets more.
"And so that's what this tax reset package is designed to do: take some of the burden off income tax and place that onto property," Wong told Reuters in an interview in August.
A basic income for residents would be a first for a developed economy. Dozens of countries have land taxes, but they usually exclude primary residences, unlike Opportunity's proposal.
National and Labour have both ruled out adopting Opportunity's tax policies, while Luxon has said dozens of times during campaigning he would not enter into coalition with Opportunity.
Wong has said she would look to negotiate with the party that secures the largest number of seats in parliament and that it would be possible to find common ground with National or Labour.
"There are different forms of us working with other parties, whether that's coalition, confidence and supply, being on the crossbenches, and all of those options are on the table for us right now," she told public broadcaster TVNZ on Saturday.
"We have to we have to look at how the votes land."
* The writer is from Reuters

Title: New Zealand preliminary vote leaves unclear who will govern
Article:
WELLINGTON: New Zealanders were unlikely to gain much clarity on Sunday over who will govern the country for the next three years, after overnight results gave the National-led coalition a slim majority,  with around 14 per cent of votes still to count.
Electoral Commission preliminary results showed coalition partners National, ACT and New Zealand First with 67 of the currently projected 131-seat parliament.
Sixty-six seats are needed for a majority.
However, the commission said special votes, around 14 per cent of the total vote, still need to be counted.
These votes include those from overseas New Zealanders and people voting outside their electorate and have historically favoured the left. These will be released with the final count on Nov 27.
Until then, the incumbent coalition will continue to operate as a caretaker government.
Neither current Prime Minister Christopher Luxon nor leader of the opposition Chris Hipkins claimed victory in their speeches following the election, which has been dominated by talk of a soft economy and the cost of living.
Simeon Brown, a National Party lawmaker and campaign chair, told public broadcaster TVNZ on Sunday that they were in "a strong position."
"We feel quite confident at this stage we can form a government, a National-led government, with our coalition partners," Brown said.
If the National-led coalition loses its majority at the official count, either it or a left-leaning coalition would require the support of the centrist Opportunity Party, which looks likely to enter parliament for the first time.
Luxon has repeatedly ruled out working with Opportunity, but Brown on Sunday did not rule out speaking with the centrist party.
Mona Krewel, a senior political science lecturer at Victoria University of Wellington, said she believed it was possible the two parties could work together.
"I actually would take them (Opportunity) for very centrist, very pragmatic, and so I do think they could make it work with National," she said.
The country switched to a mixed-member proportional system (MMP)  in 1996, meaning people vote for both a party and a local constituency candidate.
There are 71 constituency, or "electorate", seats and the Electoral Commission is currently projecting there will be 60 party list seats.
National and a minor party, Te Pati Maori, each won a disproportionately high share of constituency seats relative to their popular vote support due to tactical voting, reshaping the balance of seats in parliament and sparking debate about the electoral system, political commentator Ben Thomas said.
"It certainly looks as if we're on track for the least proportional parliament that we've had, as a result of the vagaries of the rules around how electorate seats interact with the parliament as a whole," Thomas said.
The combined support for National and Labour is at its lowest levels since the introduction of MMP, with both parties' popular vote sitting below 30 per cent.
National's low popular vote means the party is set to lose several senior lawmakers in the next parliament including Finance Minister Nicola Willis.
Brown said the party had lost some significant people, making the result "bittersweet."

Title: Smart budgeting strategies strengthen financial resilience
Article:
LETTER:
Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to maintain the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent provides some reassurance to Malaysian households, offering greater certainty in financial planning as families prepare for the year-end holidays.
For borrowers with floating-rate loans and financing, monthly repayments are likely to remain stable.
However, an unchanged OPR does not mean that living costs will remain unchanged. Prices of goods and services may continue rising even when national inflation remains relatively low.
As the year draws to a close, many families are planning their school holiday trips.
And, parents must prepare for the new school year beginning in January 2027. These overlapping expenses can place considerable pressure on household finances.
Thus, families should prioritise essential commitments before allocating money for holidays.
A good move is to set aside sufficient funds before deciding on their travel budgets, preventing financial difficulties when schools reopen.
Another good approach is for families to choose destinations that fit their budgets. Shorter trips or nearby attractions may offer equally meaningful experiences at lower costs.
Other approaches include exercising caution when using credit to finance seasonal spending and maintaining emergency savings.
A stable OPR, therefore, should be viewed as an opportunity to strengthen household financial resilience and not an invitation to borrow more or spend beyond one's means.
ASSOC PROFESSOR DR MUHAMMAD IRWAN ARIFFIN
Department of Economics
Kulliyyah of Economics and Management Sciences
International Islamic University Malaysia

Title: KTMB equipment storage facility destroyed in Sepang fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Keretapi Tanah Melayu Bhd (KTMB) storage facility in Desa Pinggiran Putra, Sepang, was 95 per cent destroyed in a fire last night.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 10.42pm, with the first fire engine arriving at the scene at 11pm.
"The fire was already raging when firefighters arrived.
"The blaze is estimated to have destroyed 95 per cent of the storage facility, but no casualties were reported," he said in a statement.
He said inspections at the scene found that the fire involved 10 containers, six transformers and several gas cylinders.
"The fire also involved a pile of cables and six diesel drums, while firefighting operations were completed at 12.50am, according to the latest report," he said.
The operation involved 17 personnel from the Dengkil fire and rescue station, assisted by personnel from the Bangi and Cyberjaya stations.

Title: Residents urge installation of traffic lights at high-risk Jalan Slim junction
Article:
TANJONG MALIM:  Residents near Perumahan Awam 3, Jalan Slim Lama here, are calling for urgent action to install traffic lights at a junction linking the Behrang Stesen-Tanjung Malim Highway (FT193) and Jalan Slim-Behrang Ulu (A121), where they claim frequent crashes, including fatal cases, have occurred.
They described the junction as a high-risk spot for road users, particularly motorcyclists, due to vehicles moving from various directions and heavy vehicles using the route.
Yameeun Marsudi, 75, who has lived in the area since 1996, said traffic lights were urgently needed to regulate traffic flow and reduce the risk of collisions between vehicles.
He said motorists travelling from Tanjong Malim who wished to enter Perumahan Awam 3 had to make a U-turn at the junction, exposing them to the risk of accidents if traffic movement was not properly controlled.
"Every time road users want to head towards Jalan Slim or make a U-turn to enter Perumahan Awam 3, navigating this junction feels like risking their lives.
"We are not asking for luxurious facilities, just a safe junction for all road users," he told Bernama when met here recently.
Meanwhile, Mohd Nizam Abdul Wahid, 44, who has lived in the area for the past 10 years, said he had frequently witnessed accidents at the junction, including several fatal incidents.
He said that about two months ago, his nephew was hit by a car coming from Tanjung Malim, which was turning into Jalan Slim, while returning home from work on a motorcycle.
"We do not want anyone else to suffer the same fate and hope traffic lights can be installed immediately," he said.
Another resident, Chong Hwee Tack, 50, who has lived in the area for 20 years, said the movement of heavy vehicles such as buses and lorries travelling downhill from Behrang Stesen was also a cause for concern.
He said these vehicles were often driven at high speeds when approaching the junction, making it difficult for other road users to enter or turn safely.
[[nid:1573131]]
"Do not wait until another fatal accident occurs before taking action. We hope the residents' request will be given serious attention, as road safety and human lives must not be taken lightly," he said.
Meanwhile, Tanjong Malim Member of Parliament Chang Lih Kang, when contacted, said applications for traffic lights, road widening and improvements to road furniture in the area had been submitted to the Perak Public Works Department in the middle of last year.
"However, to date, the funding applications for all three improvements have yet to be approved," he said.
Chang said he had also met Works Minister Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi to discuss the funding requirements and immediate measures needed to improve road safety at the junction.
He stressed that road safety must not be taken lightly and appropriate action should be taken without waiting for more accidents to occur. — BERNAMA

Title: Melaka polls: Adam Adli urges young voters to make fact-based decisions, not be swayed by sentiment
Article:
MELAKA: Young voters in the state have been urged to exercise their voting power in the 16th Melaka state election by making informed decisions based on accurate information and facts.
Melaka PKR state leadership council acting chairman, Adam Adli Abd Halim, said they should not be influenced by sentiment or politics of hate when casting their ballots on Nov 14.
He said voters aged between 18 and 39, who make up 47.34 per cent of the 687,697 registered voters in Melaka, had the power to shape the future of the state administration, and therefore should choose leaders with integrity.
"By nature when making decisions, apart from consulting our minds, we also consult our hearts on what is rational and what shapes our emotions.
"Look for what is good, and do not base our decisions on politics of hate," he said in a recent interview with Bernama.
Adam Adli said he was optimistic about Melaka's future after witnessing the active participation of the state's younger generation in the democratic process.
"The responsibility is the same regardless of whether one is young or old, but I believe young people have a different kind of energy and courage to bring about change.
"So, the state has a bright future because young people in Melaka are actively participating in democratic processes. This is your time," he said.
On PKR's candidate selection for the state election, Adam Adli said the party had adopted a more meticulous approach, fielding seven new faces out of the 10 state seats it is contesting.
He said careful assessments had been carried out to ensure that the candidates selected were suited to their respective constituencies and had strong support from grassroots machinery, while also creating opportunities for young leaders.
"For example, Farzana Hayani Mohd Nasir, the candidate for the Kelebang state seat, previously contested in Sungai Rambai, which was not her hometown.
"But now, in Kelebang, she is in her own area. She had been working there from the early stages, engaging with the community and growing up there. So, that is an improvement," he said.
Adam Adli said PKR was targeting victories in several identified seats, while also aiming to increase the number of votes it received in all the constituencies it contested compared with the 2021 Melaka state election.
He said this confidence was based on what he described as a more positive voter trend for the upcoming election compared with the previous state election, which recorded a low voter turnout of 65.85 per cent.
"We (PKR) will always aim to win in areas where we have a chance of doing so. In areas that we know are not our strongholds, we must ensure that, over time, we increase our support. If we go from 10 votes to 100, and from 100 to 1,000, we will keep building until we eventually succeed in winning," he said.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day, while early voting will take place on Nov 10. — BERNAMA

Title: Two women injured in Brickfields restaurant fire
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Two women were injured, one of whom suffered a fractured left arm, in a fire involving two double-storey restaurant premises along Jalan Tun Sambanthan in Brickfields early this morning.
Operations commander Md Fuad Selamat said the Fire and Rescue Department received an emergency call at 3.04am, with firemen arriving at the scene four minutes later.
"The fire completely destroyed the ground floor and damaged 50 per cent of the upper floor," he said in a statement.
Fuad said a 34-year-old woman sustained injuries to her right hand, while another woman, aged 24, suffered a fracture to her left arm.
"Both victims were taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for further treatment.
"The cause of the fire and the total losses incurred are still under investigation," he said.
The operation involved 35 firefighters from the Hang Tuah fire and rescue station, assisted by personnel from the Pantai and Seputeh fire stations.

Title: Fahmi joins two ministerial-level Doha forums to strengthen global digital cooperation
Article:
DOHA: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil is scheduled to take part in two ministerial-level forums today focusing on strengthening international cooperation in the development and future of the digital ecosystem.
The two events are the Ministerial Panel at Mobile World Congress (MWC) Doha 2026: Digital Leadership Forum and the International Telecommunication Union (ITU) Plenipotentiary Conference (PP-26) Ministerial Roundtable, both taking place at the Doha Exhibition and Convention Centre (DECC).
Fahmi's participation in the two forums is among the key engagements of his working visit to Doha, where he is also leading the Malaysian delegation to ITU PP-26.
According to the official programme of the Malaysian delegation, Fahmi is scheduled to attend the MWC Doha 2026 welcome ceremony before joining a ministerial panel session titled "Accelerating Cooperation for a Connected Digital Future".
The session will provide a platform for discussions on the importance of cooperation in shaping a more connected digital future.
In the afternoon, Fahmi is scheduled to attend the PP-26 Doha Ministerial Roundtable, which will feature opening remarks, ministerial presentations and a discussion session.
The programme will also see the launch of the Doha Ministerial Declaration, one of the key agenda items of the gathering.
Fahmi is also scheduled to visit exhibition booths operated by several international technology and telecommunications companies, including Huawei, Ericsson, Ooredoo, Nokia and VEON, at DECC.
In the evening, he is scheduled to attend a dinner hosted by the Global System for Mobile Communications Association (GSMA) in conjunction with MWC Doha.
Fahmi's working visit to Doha also carries an important mission for Malaysia to retain its seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term.
ITU PP-26, held in Doha, is the organisation's highest decision-making conference, convened every four years to determine its direction, policies and strategic plans.
Malaysia, which has been an ITU member since Feb 3, 1958, was elected to the ITU Council for the 2023-2026 term at the PP-22 conference in Bucharest, Romania.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: #NSTviral: Batu Caves fireworks display lights up social media [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A spectacular fireworks display over Batu Caves and surrounding areas last night has gone viral on social media, drawing thousands of reactions on Threads.
As the Indian community in Malaysia welcomed Deepavali, a two-minute-and-52-second video captured a dazzling display of fireworks illuminating the night sky, accompanied by a continuous rumble of explosions.
View on Threads
Filmed from an elevated location, the video showed fireworks of various colours lighting up the sky in a seemingly non-stop celebration.
The clip, posted by Threads user amirasyhr, has since been reposted nearly 1,000 times, garnering more than 8,400 likes, over 170 comments and more than 870 shares.
The display drew enthusiastic reactions from social media users, with many describing it as a spectacular celebration of the Festival of Lights.
One user, shariena_sarif, jokingly commented: "While other countries are busy with cyberattacks, we are busy with firecracker attacks! Happy Deepavali."
Another user, mowranaaa, said the fireworks were so loud that the noise could be heard in Klang.
"Reporting from Klang... that loud noise is not air conditioning but the thunderous sound of fireworks," the user wrote.
Meanwhile, h.aura.medina called on Malaysians to appreciate the celebrations and respect the country's cultural diversity.
"Just enjoy it. They are celebrating their festival. It happens only once a year. Let's celebrate the diversity of our races in Malaysia. Our turn will come too," the user commented.
Others praised the display, with one describing it as a true "Festival of Lights", while several extended their Deepavali greetings to the Hindu community.
Some also reminded celebrants to be considerate of their neighbours, particularly those living in residential areas, and to take precautions to prevent fireworks from damaging nearby properties.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ringgit expected to trade with slight positive bias next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to trade with a slight positive bias against the US dollar next week as investors assess the outlook for the US interest rates.
Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said investors' main focus will be on October's US Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index, scheduled for release on Tuesday and Friday respectively.
"Softer inflation readings could weigh on US Treasury yields and the greenback, providing support for the ringgit. However, stronger-than-expected inflation could reverse such gains," he told Bernama.
Domestically, Mohd Afzanizam said Malaysia's industrial production, labour market and wholesale and retail trade figures will provide further indications of Malaysia's economic resilience.
He said Bank Negara Malaysia's decision to maintain the overnight policy rate (OPR) at 2.75 per cent provides a stable policy backdrop.
"Nevertheless, trading could remain cautious as investors digest the US employment report due tonight, alongside post-midterm policy developments and geopolitical risks.
"Therefore, next week the ringgit is expected to trade within RM4.04-RM4.06 against the US dollar," he said.
Meanwhile, SPI Asset Management managing partner Stephen Innes said the ringgit could regain ground and move towards the stronger end of its trading range if the equity market selloff intensifies enough to prompt traders to price in a less hawkish stance by the US Federal Reserve.
"However, much of the direction will once again depend on crude oil and equity markets rather than domestic fundamentals. If crude oil prices remain elevated and global equities continue to face selling pressure, particularly in the semiconductor sector, the ringgit could struggle to make further gains.
"For now, investors will be watching Wall Street and oil markets for clearer direction. Until conditions in both markets stabilise, Asian currencies, including the ringgit, are likely to remain under pressure," he said
Looking ahead, Innes expects the ringgit to trade within a relatively narrow range of RM4.045 to RM4.065 against the US dollar.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit eased against the greenback to 4.0565/0610 from 4.0555/0600 a week earlier.
The local currency traded higher against a basket of other major currencies during the week.
It rose vis-a-vis the Japanese yen to 2.5616/5646 from 2.5782/5812 on the previous Friday and appreciated against the British pound to 5.4304/4365 from 5.4461/4522, and gained versus the euro to 4.5315/5365 from 4.5413/5464 a week earlier.
The ringgit traded mostly lower against Asean currencies.
It advanced versus the Singapore dollar to 3.1657/1694 from 3.1753/1791 a week earlier.
However, the local note  inched down against the Indonesian rupiah to 224.2/224.6 from 223.4/223.8, slipped vis-a-vis the Thai baht to 12.0898/1105 from 12.0373/0561 at the end of last week, and it went down against the Philippine peso to 6.43/6.44 from 6.36/6.37 previously.

Title: Mara to double number of students sent to Turkiye next year
Article:
ISTANBUL: More Malaysian students will have the opportunity to pursue higher education in Türkiye next year, with Mara planning to double its sponsorship intake.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the move was part of efforts to strengthen academic ties between the two countries.
"I will ensure that, at the very least, Mara will send twice the number of students to the same university next year," he said at a dinner with Malaysian students and Malaysian Embassy staff in Turkiye last night.
Zahid said the first batch of students are expected to prove themselves as among the best in their respective fields upon completing their four-year studies.
Meanwhile, Mara chairman Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki said the decision to send the 17 students followed discussions with the Turkish government that began in April.
He said the first batch was sent in September, following Zahid's directive for the initiative to be implemented within a short timeframe.
"These are not ordinary students. They are among the best, selected from two Mara preparatory colleges after showing outstanding achievement since the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) level," he said.
Zahid attended the dinner with the 17 Mara-sponsored students from Sabanci University.
The students are pursuing degrees in computer science and engineering, mechatronics engineering, molecular biology and bioengineering, data science, finance, materials science and electronics engineering.
Also present were Foreign Ministry deputy secretary-general (bilateral affairs) Datuk Syed Mohamad Hasrin Tengku Hussin and Malaysia's Honorary Consul in Bursa, Turkiye, Datuk Cevdet Sefer.
Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, is on a four-day working visit to Turkiye from Nov 5 to 8.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Tiong: M'sia's international safety image key to tourist confidence
Article:
SIBU: Malaysia's international safety image must be given due attention as it influences foreign tourists' confidence in visiting the country, Tourism, Arts and Culture Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said.
He said national unity was important in projecting a positive image of the country and that all parties should work towards strengthening it.
"Greater attention should be given to strengthening the economy, addressing poverty and improving the well-being of the people.
"Publicity alone cannot solve problems. We must find ways to address the people's problems," he said at the 2026 Navy Veterans Samudera Heritage Charity Gala Dinner here last night.
The event was organised by the Sarawak branch of the Royal Malaysian Navy Veterans Association (PVTLDM).
At the event, Tiong announced a contribution of RM20,000 to the association to support its efforts to look after the welfare of veterans. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia expected to trade within 1,600-1,630 range next week
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia is expected to trade within the 1,600-1,630 range next week, with selective accumulation likely to provide support at lower levels, said Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng.
He said investors would monitor the United States October Consumer Price Index and Producer Price Index figures for further clues on inflation and the Federal Reserve's interest-rate outlook.
Meanwhile, China's October inflation figures on Monday and Malaysia's September industrial production data on Tuesday would provide further insights into regional economic conditions.
"While intermittent volatility cannot be ruled out, we expect the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) to remain relatively steady," he told Bernama.
On a Friday-to-Friday basis, the FBM KLCI increased 0.98 of a point to 1,616.58 from 1,615.60 a week ago.
On the index board, the FBM Emas Index slipped 96.26 points to 11,965.47, the FBM Top 100 Index decreased 65.41 points to 11,798.45, and the FBM Emas Shariah Index sank 260.14 points to 11,822.77.
The FBM ACE Index lost 163.67 points to 5,240.24 and the FBM Mid 70 Index tumbled 399.81 points to 17,020.88.
By sector, the Energy Index dropped 57.30 points to 794.86, the Plantation Index gained 28.94 points to 8,726.36, and the Industrial Products and Services Index erased 7.02 points to 171.35.
The Financial Services Index surged 409.07 points to 18,957.06.
Weekly turnover narrowed to 15.49 billion units worth RM14.43 billion from 15.53 billion units worth RM9.97 billion in the previous week.
However, the Main Market volume jumped to 8.30 billion units valued at RM13.08 billion versus 5.13 billion units valued at RM8.83 billion previously.
Warrants turnover rose to 5.23 billion units worth RM600.74 million against 3.99 billion units worth RM608.01 million a week ago.
The ACE Market volume slid to 1.95 billion units valued at RM749.55 million from 2.07 billion units valued at RM788.72 million in the previous week.

Title: Melaka polls: Young voters crucial to BN's election hopes
Article:
MASJID TANAH: Barisan Nasional is focusing on young voters in its bid to win the Melaka election, recognising their potential to account for a significant share of the total votes.
Melaka BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh said young voters were the future leaders of the country and had an important role in determining the state's direction.
He said they should make informed choices and safeguard the progress achieved under the current administration by electing a stable and capable government.
"Young voters are being prepared to become future leaders. So, during this election, they must make the right choice.
"They must preserve what we have today so that they can build on the foundation laid by the people and choose a stable and wise government," he said.
He was speaking to reporters after a campaign ceramah for the Tanjung Bidara state constituency in Kampung Balik Batu, here last night.
Earlier, in his speech, Ab Rauf said automatic voter registration had increased the number of voters, including those who had been eligible to vote for years but had never registered.
He said the 2022 General Election had shown that BN needed to reach out to new voters and secure support beyond Umno members, particularly among young people.
Meanwhile, Ab Rauf said Muafakat Melaka, a strategic cooperation with Perikatan Nasional, could help the coalition win up to 25 seats if its campaign machinery was effectively mobilised.
"Of the 21 seats we are contesting, if we do the work properly, we can win up to 25 seats," he said.

Title: 20 injured as 5.7-magnitude earthquake strikes central Japan
Article:
TOKYO: An earthquake with a preliminary magnitude of 5.7 struck central Japan early today, injuring at least 20 people in Aichi Prefecture.
The 1.04am tremor originated in western Shizuoka Prefecture at a depth of about 40 kilometres and registered upper 5 on the Japanese seismic intensity scale in Chita, Aichi Prefecture, the Japan Meteorological Agency said.
An intensity of lower 5 was recorded in parts of Aichi, Nagano and Gifu prefectures.
The government set up a liaison office to respond to the quake.
The agency said the quake posed no tsunami risk.
Tremors were felt across neighbouring prefectures, including Yamanashi.
In Aichi Prefecture, the fire department reported that two people in Toyota City were likely injured.
Authorities urged residents in affected areas to remain vigilant, warning that aftershocks could occur in the coming days.
Meanwhile, Tohoku Shinkansen services between Tokyo and Iwate were temporarily disrupted before resuming.
Japan is situated along the Pacific Ring of Fire, an area characterised by frequent seismic and volcanic activity.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: M'sian diaspora in Qatar conducts evacuation drills for war threats
Article:
DOHA, (Qatar): The Malaysian diaspora in Qatar is taking proactive steps to strengthen emergency preparedness by conducting evacuation drills, including simulations involving war and nuclear threats.
Malaysian Ambassador to Qatar Faizal Razali said the initiatives, organised by the Malaysian community through the Malaysian Association in Qatar (MAQ), also involved Malaysians in Bahrain as part of preparations for possible security crises in the region.
He said MAQ, which brings together about 30 community clubs, played an important role as a support network for the Malaysian Embassy, particularly in assisting Malaysians during crises.
"MAQ, together with the community leaders and appointed focal points, has successfully helped the embassy manage about 6,000 Malaysians during crises, including arranging their evacuation and return to Malaysia," he said at a gathering between Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and the Malaysian diaspora here yesterday.
Faizal said MAQ also organised various interactive activities, including talks and online concerts, to help ease the anxiety of Malaysians during crises.
He said about 6,200 Malaysians lived in Qatar, working in various professional and essential sectors, and described the community as one of the most active, well-organised and patriotic Malaysian communities in the region.
Faizal also expressed appreciation to community leaders and appointed focal points for their commitment to supporting the embassy in looking after the welfare of Malaysians.
"Malaysians in Qatar are among the most disciplined, supportive of one another and patriotic, and they always uphold Malaysia's good name.
"Even the Qatari government holds our people in high regard and recognises their expertise," he said.
Faizal said the spirit of unity among Malaysians in Qatar was also strengthened through the organisation of the Malaysia Qatar Games, featuring 16 sports, adding that a recent dragon boat event attracted about 200 participants, with total attendance, including spectators, reaching approximately 500.
The Malaysia Business Associations Council had also been established to promote economic cooperation between Malaysia and Qatar, while the Qampung youth association remained active in social, cultural and patriotic activities.
Faizal said Fahmi's visit to Doha also helped strengthen ties between Malaysians living abroad and the government, despite their distance from home.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Edwin John Clement Henry, 49, said access to accurate and reliable information was important to prevent confusion, particularly amid geopolitical tensions in West Asia and the spread of rumours on social media.
Edwin, who has lived in Qatar since 2007, said there was a perception among people back home that Malaysians in the country were unsafe and needed to be evacuated.
[[nid:1573120]]
However, he said this did not reflect the situation he and his family were experiencing in Qatar.
"I can say that we feel safe despite these geopolitical issues. My family and I feel very safe here," said Edwin, who is from Selangor.
An active MAQ member, Edwin said face-to-face engagements with government leaders were important as they allowed the diaspora to obtain direct clarification on current developments and government policies.
He said the meeting with the Communications Minister also provided an opportunity for Malaysians abroad to raise issues affecting their daily lives, including the government's efforts to strengthen child protection against paedophilia and online crimes. — BERNAMA

Title: Clashes erupt in Paris as thousands join fresh protests across France
Article:
PARIS: Thousands of people protested across France Saturday in a new show of anger against the government with clashes erupting between police and some protesters in Paris despite a lower turnout than on previous weeks.
The protests marked the fourth consecutive weekend of demonstrations against the rising cost of living which have erupted as the country heads to presidential elections in five months' time where the far right sees its best chance yet to win power.
A total of 146,000 people took part in demonstrations across France on Saturday, including 46,000 in Paris, the interior ministry said. Unions put the figure at 250,000 protesters nationwide, with 75,000 in the capital.
These figures were lower than the previous three weekends of protests but also came after a mass union protest on Thursday that rallied 575,000 people according to the authorities – 1.6 million according to unions.
At the end of the protest in Paris, police used tear gas against individuals throwing projectiles and homemade fireworks at the security forces, an AFP correspondent said.
Police said a group of 200 violent individuals attacked officers as they were arresting a man who had set fire to a trash bin in the square.
- BANNED PROTESTS THWARTED -
Some 70,000 members of the security forces were deployed Saturday, ready to move in quickly after mass protests on Oct 17 degenerated into the worst riots seen in France in years.
Unions had staged a march along a traditional route, from the Place de la Republique in central Paris to Place de la Nation in the east of the city where the clashes erupted at the end of the protest.
But the Yellow Vests movement – a group whose protests shook Emmanuel Macron in the early years of his presidency almost a decade ago – called for a rival demonstration at the Place de la Concorde in central Paris, a stone's throw from the president's Elysee Palace and the lower house of parliament.
This action has been banned by the authorities, and on Saturday a large police presence prevented protesters from getting close. Some 100 people who arrived were surrounded by police and one of the movement's coordinators, Benjamin Ball, and its spokeswoman, Azelma Sigaux, were among those arrested by police, an AFP reporter said.
In the southeastern city of Lyon, police fired tear gas to disperse several hundred people in the city centre blocking a road during an unauthorised gathering.
- 'THIS CAN'T GO ON' -
The wave of demonstrations was sparked by a movement in late September by high school students angered by conditions at their establishments. These teens, joined by university students, remain at the heart of the protests.
"Today is a date that helps keep the pressure on," said Sabine Kharbach, spokeswoman of the Student Union. "Many young people are mobilising because the government's responses remain unsatisfactory."
The police response has faced criticism for being heavy-handed, with dozens of internal investigations launched into allegations of brutality against demonstrators.
Local businesses are also feeling the pain. "So this can't go on, otherwise I think it will be a disaster before long," said Paris shop manager Jean Emile Moulinier. His store is around the main protest route and he said hardly any customers brave security barricades on protest weekends.
Shop windows of stores in Paris and other cities were again barricaded with wooden shutters and often closed for the day to prevent potential ransacking.
The government is grappling with ways to find solutions but is constrained by France's gigantic debt pile, which is already spooking markets.
Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu is to meet unions and employer federation representatives on Monday to discuss wages and purchasing power.
But student and teacher groups in France have called for a new strike on Tuesday to keep pressure on the government for more education spending, saying they were "in a position of strength (and) the government in a position of weakness and starting to yield."
Polls indicate that far-right candidate Marine Le Pen is the favourite to win the Elysee in 2027 with her main rival currently not one of Macron's centrist former allies but hard-left leader Jean-Luc Melenchon.
Melenchon, addressing 20,000 at a rally outside Paris Saturday, declared "we are going to win" and "everything must change."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Iran claims its forces are 'stronger' than at start of war
Article:
TEHERAN: Iran said on Saturday its military had grown stronger since the outset of the war with the United States, as mediators including Qatar worked to prevent any return to fighting after months of deadlock in the conflict.
Washington also offered a US$20 million reward for information about Teheran's nuclear programme.
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on Instagram on Saturday that over the past 48 hours he held phone calls with ministers from 12 countries.
US President Donald Trump, meanwhile, called Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani on Friday to discuss efforts to end the war.
Qatar's Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani applauded colleagues in the US administration for "genuine intentions to find a way to contain the situation and to de-escalate it."
"Thanks also to some wise voices in Teheran, we have prevented that from getting out of control," he said in Oxford on Friday.
Trump said Iran – which he stressed has had its economy and military severely damaged over eight months of war – is eager to end the conflict.
"We're dealing with them now. They want to make a deal very badly," he said.
The US leader previously talked up the possibility of resuming heavy strikes on Iran but has since walked back from the idea.
Nevertheless, the US military has conducted occasional limited strikes.
Late on Saturday, the official IRNA news agency reported two explosions on the island of Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz, hours after two earlier explosions were reported and the military said it had shot down a drone over the island.
Washington last attacked Qeshm on Tuesday.
- NO 'PERFECT DEAL' -
The Middle East conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Teheran has since sought to limit traffic through Hormuz, which normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption.
Iranian army spokesman Mohammad Akraminia said the strategic waterway would remain closed until Teheran's demands were met by Washington.
He also said Iran's forces "are on higher alert and are stronger than they were at the beginning of the war."
"They now possess greater motivation, commitment and self-confidence," he added, state news agency IRNA reported on Saturday.
"Under the order of the Supreme Leader, the response of the armed forces will be immediate, effective and without geographical limitations."
Revolutionary Guards spokesman Hossein Mohebbi told Fars news agency on Saturday that "the increase in the range of Iran's missiles continues steadily."
He spoke days after Trump's Republican Party suffered heavy losses in midterm elections widely viewed as a referendum on the US leader's turbulent second term.
Ali Vaez, of the International Crisis Group, told AFP that "having suffered electoral defeat and failed to secure military victory, Trump is unlikely to tolerate the trifecta of diplomatic humiliation."
"The midterms have raised the political cost of war, but a lame duck Trump could become a flame duck if Iran denies him a face-saving exit," he added.
"Both sides may be mistaking the other's weakness for a reason to hold out rather than compromise."
Qatar's prime minister said "we cannot... just wait for this moment of a perfect deal" as there would never be one.
He added that priority should be given to addressing the nuclear issue and ensuring freedom of navigation and the security of the Gulf.
- REWARD OFFERED -
Iran's military said in a statement carried by state TV on Saturday that a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz "caught fire and came to a halt after striking a naval mine."
The US had recently said all mines had been cleared from the waterway.
On Friday, the US military said it was offering a US$20 million reward "and possible relocation" for information about Iran's nuclear programme.
Rewards for Justice, a State Department programme, was seeking information on topics including "facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community," US Central Command said on X.
Trump has repeatedly said US forces have effectively obliterated Iran's nuclear programme.
"If we didn't hit Iran, you wouldn't have Israel today," he said on Friday.
"If they had nuclear, they would have used nuclear. They would have obliterated the Middle East."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Eisenkot tasked with forming government in bid to oust Netanyahu
Article:
JERUSALEM: Israel's president announced on Saturday he would task Gadi Eisenkot with forming the next government following last week's election, in what Netanyahu's rivals see as a first step to remove the country's longest-serving prime minister.
The opposition bloc led by Eisenkot, a former military chief and political newcomer who has tried to appeal to secular and liberal Israelis, has opened the door to a once improbable alliance with ultra-Orthodox Jews, which could give it the numbers to form a coalition.
President Isaac Herzog said that after consultations with all parties during the week, he would grant Eisenkot the first chance to form a government after the Oct 27 election, in which neither side secured a majority in a country deeply polarised by Netanyahu's hard-right rule and worn down by three years of war.
The formal appointment would take place in an official ceremony on Sunday at the president's residence in Jerusalem, Herzog's office said.
Eisenkot, who later pledged to "do everything" to form a new government, was recommended by parties representing 67 lawmakers as opposed to 46 for Netanyahu's bloc.
But the recommendations for Eisenkot included members of Israel's Arab minority – whose seat haul soared in the election on the back of anger against Netanyahu – and right-leaning segments of the opposition that are against relying on Arab votes.
- UNITY GOVERNMENT -
Herzog, originally from Israel's now defunct left-wing Labour Party but who has a non-partisan role and has forged a working relationship with Netanyahu, has signalled that he would like to explore a national unity government that would seek to bring together Jewish Israelis from across the political spectrum.
Pressure for a unity government could build if Netanyahu follows through on threats to resume war on Iran, although US President Donald Trump has not given the green light.
Netanyahu, who has led Israel on and off for nearly two decades and guided its sharply rightward turn in recent years, faces corruption charges and potentially jail if he leaves office. He also faces an arrest warrant over the Gaza war from the International Criminal Court, whose authority he rejects.
Netanyahu has already called for a unity government but the opposition has stood firm on removing him first.
He has attacked opposition leaders for even considering working with Israeli Arabs, descendants of Palestinians who stayed after the creation of Israel in 1948.
The incumbent premier said on Saturday that a potential coalition between opposition parties and Arab lists, would "dismantle the State of Israel from within" and urged the formation of a unity government comprising "all the Zionist parties that want to safeguard our state."
In response, Eisenkot's Yashar party urged Netanyahu's allies and members of his Likud party to form a unity government led by Eisenkot and to "publicly announce the dissolution of their alliance with the extremists."
"Now is the time to form a national emergency government," Eisenkot wrote on X in his first reaction to the announcement of his designation. "I will do everything to ensure we are worthy."
Opposition bloc member Avigdor Liberman, a former Netanyahu aide turned fierce critic who nonetheless shares his hawkish views on the Palestinians, has made clear that he will not sit with Eisenkot if he relies on Israeli-Arab votes.
But on Friday, Liberman – a staunch secularist whose support base initially was Russian-speaking immigrants – made a U-turn on another group he had shunned and said he was open to discussions on a law that would enshrine an exemption for ultra-Orthodox Jews from mandatory military service.
Liberman and another opposition leader, Naftali Bennett, had made closing the exemption a core campaign promise and had viscerally criticised ultra-Orthodox Jews as burdens on the state, responding to wide resentment by other Israelis at a time when reservists are serving multiple tours in Gaza and Lebanon.
Eisenkot has proposed requiring national service for all Israelis but allowing citizens to choose a civilian option rather than the military, opening the door to integrating the ultra-Orthodox.
On Friday, Eisenkot said it was urgent to replace Netanyahu, calling him a threat to the "very existence of Israeli democracy."
Following his appointment, Eisenkot will have 28 days to come up with the 61 votes needed for a government. If he comes up short, Herzog can provide a 14-day extension before he has to offer the mandate to someone else.
If neither side succeeds, Israel will head to fresh elections. The country held five elections between 2019 and 2022 due to repeated deadlocks.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump asks Justice Department to investigate Democrats over impeachment threats
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was ordering the Justice Department to examine Democratic threats to impeach members of his administration.
Trump faces a radically transformed and hostile political landscape after Democrats seized both the House of Representatives and the Senate in Tuesday's midterms.
Democrats have vowed investigations into Trump and senior members of his administration, including Attorney General Todd Blanche and Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth.
"The Democrats are going around threatening a lot of people," Trump said in a post on his Truth Social platform.
"This is extortion at the highest level, and they should be held accountable," he said, arguing that there had been "no impeachable acts committed."
Trump said he was ordering the Justice Department to "look into this criminal act" and said "imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS."
With control of committees in both chambers, Democrats can summon officials, demand documents and hold public hearings, potentially putting Trump and his senior aides under intense scrutiny.
Likely subjects include the Trump family's business and cryptocurrency dealings, government contracts involving billionaire Elon Musk, cuts to federal agencies, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war.
"Lawyer up," wrote incoming House Oversight Committee chairman Robert Garcia on X as the results became clear on election night.
Democrats have also signaled interest in the handling of files relating to notorious sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
The administration could resist demands for testimony or documents, triggering court battles.
Democrats could pursue Trump's third impeachment, though party leaders have not committed to doing so.
The House needs only a simple majority to impeach, but removing a president requires a two-thirds vote in the Senate – far beyond the party's numbers.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gunman 'fascinated by far-right' kills six in Poland
Article:
KRAKÓW: Six people were killed and at least 15 wounded on Saturday when a gunman opened fire in the landmark historic centre of Poland's second city of Krakow, in the country's deadliest shooting in decades.
Three bodies – of two women and a man – were later found at the suspect's home, Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said, adding there was "much to suggest that they are members of the (suspect's) immediate family."
Tusk also announced Poland would hold two days of mourning over the shooting that he called an act of "terrorism."
Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski said the gunman appeared to be "fascinated by far-right ideologies."
A British national was among the killed, according to Polish police chief, Marek Boron, and five foreigners were among the wounded in hospital, the authorities said.
"Two people who have not yet been identified," Boron said referring to the victims killed.
Britain's Prime Minister Andy Burnham said he was "shocked and saddened by the appalling shooting."
"My thoughts are with the families of those who have lost their lives, everyone injured and all those affected by this senseless violence," he wrote on X.
The suspect – a Polish citizen born in 2002 – drove a car onto Krakow's Main Market Square and began shooting at random people, said police.
Two officers were wounded as they tried to stop the man, the police said, before shooting the suspect who was later detained and taken to a hospital.
An AFP reporter at the scene saw ambulances and multiple police cars as police cordoned off the area – one of Poland's landmark tourist hotspots popular with locals and foreign visitors.
"Everything suggests that the perpetrator held very, very radical views. A number of weapons were found in the car he was driving," Kierwinski said.
"Everything suggests that he was fascinated by far-right ideologies" and held "ultra-nationalist views," he added.
The man was wearing military-style clothing at the time of the attack, said Kierwinski.
- TUSK PRAISES 'HEROIC' POLICE -
Andrzej Fijolek, spokesman for the chief of police, said the attacker had used a semi-automatic rifle similar to the American AR-15.
The authorities have not yet disclosed the nationalities of all the victims of the attack, Poland's deadliest shooting since the fall of communism in 1989.
"Our highest praise goes to the heroic police officers who risked their lives in the line of duty," Tusk said.
On Saturday evening, AFP reporters saw the usually bustling Main Market Square sealed off, with heavily armed police and forensic investigators inspecting the site of the attack.
Witnesses told AFP they saw people take refuge in shops and restaurants in the surrounding streets.
"I saw a man shooting at people and walking around the square," Annette, a woman in her sixties, told AFP.
"It's a tragedy for Krakow, we've never seen anything like this before," she added.
"It's very frightening to think that there are still risks in Europe – risks of a terrorist nature," Stella, a 22-year-old tourist from Rennes, northwest France, told AFP.
- 'DRAMATIC EVENTS' -
Deadly shootings are extremely rare in Poland, a European Union and Nato member of 38 million people.
But the country has been on high alert following a series of stabbings in October, which Tusk denounced as a "cult of violence."
Warsaw, a staunch ally of Ukraine since Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022, has repeatedly warned of Russian sabotage and hybrid warfare on Polish soil, accusations rejected by Moscow.
Poland is also seeing a sharp rise in the number of firearms licences. In 2025, more than 50,000 new licences were issued, bringing the total to 411,000, according to police figures.
The historic city of Krakow in southern Poland was once the country's capital and attracts millions of tourists every year.
In 2025, it was visited by 16.2 million people.
Poland's conservative-nationalist president Karol Nawrocki said on X he was awaiting "a full explanation of the circumstances surrounding these dramatic events."
"The safety of Poles is an absolute priority," he added.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy offered his condolences, saying that "Ukraine stands in solidarity with Poland and the Polish people. People have the right to safety."
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said on X that "Germany stands shoulder to shoulder with Poland as a friend and partner during these difficult times."
The EU's top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, described the shooting as "a tragedy that will be felt far beyond Poland."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: King Charles open to China visit, but palace says it would be carefully considered
Article:
LONDON: A British monarch has only ever made one state visit to China: Queen Elizabeth II four decades ago. King Charles III would consider undertaking the second, according to an aide.
"If the government said, 'Will the king go to China?' I think, you know we think about it very carefully," a senior palace aide told reporters this week.
The late queen, Charles's mother, visited China with her husband Prince Philip in October 1986.
The trip included stops in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou, according to reports at the time.
It came two years after the signing of the Sino-British Joint Declaration setting out the terms for the return of Hong Kong, which improved relations between the two countries.
"This is the 40th anniversary of the last state visit," noted the aide, speaking at the end of the king's nine-day tour of the Caribbean.
Charles's trip was dominated by the thorny subject of slavery reparations. He called the transatlantic slave trade a "monstrous injustice" as the UK government mulls an apology.
"I think what we're seeing is a very clear pattern emerging of the government asking the king to head into quite politically charged situations, quite challenging situations," said the aide.
The king, who is politically neutral, "relishes" the "tough parts" of his role and can be a "great secret weapon" for the government, the aide added.
"Whether that's leading on the environment, whether it's renewing and refreshing and reinvigorating relationships with nations where there have been some complex political issues at play, that is what he lives and breathes for," they said.
Charles, who is nearly 78 and still being treated for an undisclosed cancer, was widely praised for his state visit to the United States and delicate handling of US President Donald Trump earlier this year.
Relations between London and Beijing have been strained for years, fuelled in part by tensions over the political situation in former British colony Hong Kong, criticism of Beijing's human rights record and spying allegations.
But UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is now pursuing the same policy of cautious rapprochement started by his predecessor Keir Starmer, who visited Beijing in January.
"China is a hugely important country. It's a very complex country. It would pose you know a lot of complexity in putting a program together," Charles's aide said.
As then prince of Wales, Charles oversaw Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule as Britain's most senior representative at the 1997 handover alongside China's then president Jiang Zemin.
Asked whether Burnham would be asking the king to visit China, his spokesman told AFP that questions about the monarch's travel was "one for the palace."--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Pope Leo condemns violence, child deaths in Uruguay's crime-hit neighbourhood
Article:
MONTEVIDEO: Pope Leo XIV on Saturday slammed the deaths of children in areas of wealthy Uruguay gripped by drug violence, as he visited the most crime-ridden neighborhood in the South American country.
Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of the continent where he served nearly two decades as a missionary.
Leo walked amid high security through the streets of the Casavalle area of  Montevideo, where the murder rate is four times the national average. Residents say they hear gunfire every night.
"There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home," the pope said.
"In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives," he said.
Violence is on the rise in traditionally safe Uruguay, due to its growing role as a hub in Latin America's cocaine trade.
Tit-for-tat attacks by gangs vying for control of drug routes have caused the murder rate to spiral.
Katherine Silva's voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child.
After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she "went through very dark times" and "nearly died" before being saved by a Catholic family.
- 'CHANGE LIVES' -
Claudia, a 33-year-old nurse who did not wish to give her surname, described to AFP once seeing a motorcycle pull up in front of her house "and riddle someone with bullets."
"You don't know what to do when your children see a body lying there. It's become very normalised," she said.
As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.
"Being here with you makes me feel at home, and brings back memories of the visits I made to various communities as a missionary," Leo told the crowd.
Federico Castro, 29, said he hoped the pope's visit would change the lives of people like him who "made bad decisions."
"I've stopped walking those paths of evil and death," he said, crediting his faith for turning his life around.
There are a disproportionate number of young men among murder victims, official figures show, with experts suggesting many youths are being lured into crime as a way to make money.
Some four in 10 children and adolescents live in poverty in Uruguay, according to UNICEF.
Paint shop owner Mario Tabarez said he doubted the pope's visit would have a long-term effect.
"The addicts have disappeared this week, but once this is all over, they'll be back on the streets," he told AFP.
- BUILD BRIDGES -
Leo started the second day of his South American tour calling on Catholics in the secular country to be "bridge builders" for the faith.
Latin America is the world's most Catholic continent but the number of people who define themselves as such has plummeted in the past 30 years, from 80 per cent to 55 per cent, a Latinobarometro poll showed.
In the northwestern city of Paysandu, Leo paid homage to the local tradition of sharing the herbal infusion called mate, sipped from a gourd with a metal straw.
Mate "teaches us to share and be together," the pope told thousands of faithful, many of whom were clutching one of the hot drinks.
"Mate has even made its way to Rome," Leo joked.
At the Catholic University of Uruguay, he returned to a key theme of his papacy: the importance of ensuring AI is put at the service of human dignity.
The pope warned of "dehumanisation" through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the "person before the algorithm."
On Friday, in the first speech of his tour, Leo advocated for universal health care.
His own lung cancer diagnosis made him think of the "many men and women" who do not receive a timely diagnosis or treatment, he said.
US-born Leo's tour had been in doubt after he was diagnosed with a cancerous tumor, but on the flight from Rome to Montevideo he cheerfully told journalists he was "in fairly good shape."
His tour will take him to Argentina, home of the late Pope Francis, on Sunday and then to Peru, where he served as bishop and which claims the pope as one of its own.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Trump offers press secretary role to UFC chief Dana White
Article:
WASHINGTON: US President Donald Trump said Saturday he was offering a press secretary role to mixed martial arts executive and "violent fighter" Dana White.
"I am pleased to announce that the Great Dana White, a violent Fighter and Warrior, has been offered the job of Press Secretary of the United States," Trump wrote on his Truth Social account.
"Dana, please take the job!" he said.
While White did not explicitly accept the job, the Ultimate Fighting Championship (UFC) boss posted a photo – possibly AI-generated – that showed him behind the lectern in the White House press briefing room, captioned "On to the next chapter."
The White House has been without a press secretary since Oct 16 when Katie Zacharia left the position after less than a week on the job.
White, 57, is president and CEO of the UFC, the largest and most successful organisation in the world of mixed martial arts. UFC's violent cage fights are broadcast across the globe.
Trump also listed six UFC fighters that he hoped White would bring to the White House as advisers, "even though some are not from our Country."
Two of the fighters mentioned are Russian and one is Brazilian.
The White House amplified the announcement by publishing a screenshot of the president's post on one of its official accounts.
Trump and White are old friends, and Trump has often tried to associate his MAGA brand of politics with the hugely popular UFC.
On his 80th birthday in June, UFC held a bloody cage match on the White House South Lawn. He has also attended bouts in Miami, New York and New Jersey since winning his second White House term.
When Trump won reelection in 2024, White appeared alongside the Republican for his victory speech.
Since Trump's reelection, White has joined the board of directors of Meta, which many saw as a sign of the tech company's conservative shift.--AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Gardenia probes complaints over products
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Gardenia Bakeries (KL) Sdn Bhd is investigating complaints from consumers following claims on social media that several children had fallen ill after consuming its products.
The company said it took the reports seriously and was concerned about the well-being of the consumers and families involved.
In a statement, the company said its team had met with one of the consumers concerned to better understand the reported incident and obtain further information.
It had also collected the relevant products for examination as part of its ongoing investigation.
"The relevant departments are reviewing the available information, production records and quality controls to establish the facts and determine the appropriate course of action," it said.
The controversy emerged after a woman's post on Threads about her two sons experiencing vomiting after allegedly consuming Gardenia products gained traction, prompting other parents to share similar experiences.
She had asked whether there could have been changes to the products' ingredients, formulations or manufacturing processes.
Gardenia, meanwhile, said that there had been no such changes.
"We would also like to reassure our consumers that there have been no changes to our product recipes or formulations, and that our established food safety and quality control procedures remain in place," it said.
The company also pledged to cooperate fully with the Health Ministry in any further investigations, including inspections at its factories.
"Gardenia KL is committed to providing safe and high-quality products to our consumers," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Elderly couple killed after car skids into drain on Plus Highway
Article:
SEREMBAN: An elderly couple died after the car they were travelling in skidded into a drain at KM242 of the southbound North-South Expressway (PLUS) Saturday afternoon.
Rembau police chief Superintendent Ngiam Ooi Ming said the 75-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene, while his 70-year-old wife died while receiving treatment at Tuanku Ja'afar Hospital at 8pm.
"Preliminary investigations found that the Proton Saga carrying the couple was driven by a 20-year-old man, with another passenger, a 21-year-old woman. They were travelling from Cheras, Kuala Lumpur, to Port Dickson.
"On reaching the scene, a group of motorcyclists riding in convoy are believed to have overtaken and suddenly moved into the car's path, causing it to lose control and skid into a drain on the left side of the highway," he said in a statement tonight.
Ngiam said the female passenger was seriously injured and receiving treatment at Rembau Hospital, while the driver was unhurt.
Police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and are tracing the group of motorcyclists believed to have been at the scene.
Ngiam also urged members of the public who witnessed the incident or have dashcam footage to contact the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Rembau police headquarters to assist with the investigation.
– BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Five killed in shooting in main square of Polish city of Krakow
Article:
WARSAW: Five people have died and more than 10 have been injured in a shooting on the main market square in Krakow, police said on Saturday.
"The perpetrator was shot by police officers and is currently being transported to a hospital," police wrote on X.
A police spokesperson told Reuters that they began to receive reports about 3pm (1400 GMT) that a car from which shots were being fired at random people had entered the square.

Title: Cabinet ministers, state leaders extend Deepavali wishes
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Several cabinet ministers have extended Deepavali greetings to those celebrating, calling on the public to preserve unity, harmony, and wellbeing.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek expressed hope that the meaningful festival would offer families an opportunity to spend quality time together and strengthen familial bonds.
"To the entire Hindu community in Malaysia, especially teachers, students, and the wider education fraternity, I extend my heartfelt wishes that this festival brings lasting happiness and wellbeing," she said in a Facebook post.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the festive season is an ideal platform for mutual visits and fostering ties across ethnic and cultural lines.
"Amid the vibrant celebrations, prioritise personal health by observing a balanced diet. Cut down on sugar in drinks, and share more sweet smiles. For those returning to their hometowns or visiting relatives, drive carefully to ensure a safe journey," he said.
Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari said he hoped the festival tomorrow would bring peace, prosperity, and joy to Hindu Malaysians, while advising motorists to drive cautiously when travelling back to their hometowns.
Meanwhile, Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo, in a Facebook post, said he hoped that the auspicious celebration of Deepavali in Malaysia would bring happiness, peace, and renewed hope to all Malaysians.
He also urged the public to embrace cultural and religious diversity as a foundation to foster unity, affection, and mutual respect.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali hoped the celebration would bring joy, wellbeing, and prosperity to the Hindu community celebrating with family and loved ones.
