Title: RM1,000 lifeline: Sabah taxi drivers get first-ever cash aid as passengers dwindle
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 8 — The one-off RM1,000 Special Financial Assistance under Budget 2027 has come as a relief to taxi drivers in Sabah, whose daily earnings have dwindled amid growing competition from other modes of transport.
Azizarjan Japar, 43, a mother of four, said competition from newer transport services had left many conventional taxi drivers going entire days without picking up a single passenger.
The assistance would therefore go a long way in helping them cope with their daily expenses.
Having worked as a taxi driver for more than 10 years, she hoped the authorities would continue to strengthen the service to ensure it remained relevant in the state’s transport network.
She said the cash assistance would also provide some financial breathing space for women drivers like herself as they grappled with the rising cost of living.
“The assistance has eased the burden on my family, especially in meeting my children’s school and daily expenses.
“However, in the long term, we need to find ways to ensure the taxi service continues to be strengthened,” she told Bernama.
She was speaking after a ceremony to distribute the assistance to 1,105 taxi, rental car and school bus drivers in Sabah, officiated by Sabah Commercial Vehicle Licensing Board (LPKP) chairman Datuk Phoong Jin Zhe here recently (November 6).
Sabah taxi drivers (from left) Erwandy Rani, Azizarjan Japar and Abdul Patta Anbotika receiving the Special Financial Assistance for taxi drivers at the state-level presentation in Kota Kinabalu on November 6, 2026. to— Bernama pic
The special cash assistance was announced by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim when tabling Budget 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat last month as part of efforts to channel the country’s wealth directly to the people.
Veteran taxi driver Erwandy Rani, 64, who has been driving a taxi full-time since 1984, described the assistance as a meaningful recognition of his more than four decades of service on the road.
“Nowadays, there is hardly any income.
“Sometimes I get only two trips in an entire week, and the fares are not even enough to cover the cost of fuel,” he said.
He said the sharp decline in passenger numbers had forced drivers to pay for their own fuel without earning enough to offset the expense.
Erwandy said he was grateful to receive the assistance, the first of its kind he had received from the government, at a time when taxi drivers were facing increasing financial pressure.
Another driver, Abdul Patta Anbotika, 55, said the difference between taxi drivers’ earnings in the past and today was stark, reflecting changes in the public transport landscape.
“I am very grateful for the government’s assistance because our earnings as taxi drivers have fallen significantly compared with the past,” he said.
He said that when he started driving a taxi in 1997, he could earn up to RM200 a day in the city, but now even making RM100 a day was difficult.
The more than 50 per cent drop in daily earnings has tested the resilience of conventional taxi drivers, who often have to wait for hours at taxi stands just to pick up a passenger, he said.
He described the assistance as a sign that the government had not overlooked the plight of veteran drivers who continued to work hard to earn a living. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: LPKP stands for Lembaga Pelesenan Kenderaan Perdagangan in Malay.

Title: Ships, defence and halal: What Zahid discussed with Turkiye’s consul in Bursa
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 8 — The potential to develop a ship maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) hub in Bagan Datuk, Perak, was among the main topics discussed at a meeting between Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and Malaysia’s Honorary Consul in Bursa, Turkiye, Datuk Cevdet Sefer, here yesterday.
At the 30-minute meeting, which began at 11am local time (4pm in Malaysia), Ahmad Zahid said Malaysia had domestic shipping industry capabilities and had attracted interest from foreign investors seeking opportunities in Bagan Datuk, with participation from Turkiye among those receiving attention.
He said Universiti Kuala Lumpur Malaysian Institute of Marine Engineering Technology (UniKL Mimet) in Lumut had also been identified as having the potential to support the maritime industry through its expertise in marine engineering, naval architecture and maritime management.
Ahmad Zahid said the meeting also covered opportunities for transferring Turkiye’s technological expertise, building local industrial capacity and expanding cooperation in high-value sectors with the potential to benefit both countries’ economies.
“Potential cooperation in the defence and security industries, including the development of light defence systems, technology transfer and local production of components in Malaysia, with Pahang or Sarawak proposed as project locations, was also discussed,” he said here yesterday.
In the financial sector, Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said both sides explored opportunities to share Malaysia’s expertise in Islamic banking, Syariah-compliant financing and the sukuk market, as well as potential cooperation in green financing.
“Malaysia’s potential as an investment destination for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and high-tech data centres was also discussed, with a stable supply of energy and water identified as among the key factors in attracting investment.
“In the halal industry, discussions focused on expanding cooperation beyond food and beverages to pharmaceuticals, cosmetics, vaccines, Islamic banking, takaful and high-value halal products,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid is in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8, in conjunction with his participation in the TRT World Forum 2026 at the Istanbul Congress Centre (ICC), which began yesterday and runs for two days. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain floods parts of Central Seberang Perai, fallen trees hit cars and homes
Article:
BUKIT MERTAJAM, Nov 8 — Heavy rain yesterday evening has caused flooding in several areas in Central Seberang Perai, while two separate incidents involving fallen trees damaged vehicles and part of a building structure in the district.
The Central Seberang Perai District Disaster Management Committee secretariat said the affected areas included Seberang Jaya, Permatang Rawa, Tanah Liat, Mengkuang Titi and Jalan Baru, following heavy rain that began at about 4.30pm.
It said several homes were also affected by rising water, while drainage problems were reported around Seberang Jaya, although the situation remained under control.
“At 7.30pm, we received reports of rising water levels in Mengkuang Titi, and the relevant agencies immediately continued monitoring the situation and liaising with the local community.
“The Social Welfare Department is also on standby in the event that residents need to be evacuated,” it said in a statement last night.
However, based on reports as of 8pm, no temporary relief centres (PPS) had been opened, while periodic monitoring continued in flood-prone areas in the event of prolonged heavy rain.
Meanwhile, Penang Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division Assistant Director John Sagun Francis said two incidents involving fallen trees were reported in Perai and Mengkuang Titi yesterday evening, but no casualties were reported.
He said that in an incident near Desa Sutera Square, Perai, a tree fell onto a Proton Saga taxi parked in the area and damaged a small section of the roof structure of a nearby shop.
He said the department received a distress call at 6.01 pm before deploying seven personnel from the Perai Fire and Rescue Station, assisted by personnel from the Bandar Perda station, to the scene.
“Tree-cutting and clearance work was carried out at the scene with assistance from the Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP), before the operation ended at 7.57pm,” he said.
In a separate incident in Mengkuang Titi, Kubang Semang, John said a tree fell onto a Perodua Bezza and part of a house.
He said six personnel from the Penanti Fire and Rescue Station were deployed to the scene after receiving a call at 6.01pm to carry out tree-cutting and clearance work.
He said the scene was subsequently handed over to the house owner after checks confirmed that there were no further hazards, before the operation ended at 6.48 pm. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: PPS stands for Pusat Pemindahan Sementara in Malay while MBSP stands for Majlis Bandaraya Seberang Perai.

Title: Police round up nine suspects after 19-year-old killed in Sibu
Article:
SIBU, Nov 8 — Police have detained nine individuals aged between 16 and 42 to assist in investigations into the murder of a 19-year-old who is believed to have been stabbed during a fight at a public park in Jalan Gambir here early yesterday.
Sibu district police chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad said all suspects were rounded up at several locations around Sibu between 10am and 4pm today following intelligence gathering and investigations by the Sibu District Police Headquarters Criminal Investigation Department (CID).
He said police received a report at about 2 am regarding a brawl where the complainant was assaulted by a group of people.
“During the incident, a young man was believed to have been stabbed with a sharp weapon and was confirmed dead by a medical team from Sibu Hospital,” he said in a statement last night.
Abang Zainal Abidin added that the incident had also gone viral on Facebook.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder, which provides for the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, and not less than 12 strokes of the cane, upon conviction.
Police have also urged members of the public with information on the incident to come forward to assist in the investigation.
Earlier, the youth was reported to have died after he was believed to have been stabbed in the chest with a sharp weapon in the incident at about midnight. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: ACP stands for Assistant Commissioner of Police.

Title: Two hours of rain, one closed bridge: Subang’s Kampung Melayu hit by flash floods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — Heavy rain that lasted for about two hours caused flash flooding in Kampung Melayu Subang and Jalan Jati Bridge that spans Sungai Damansara has been closed due to erosion along the riverbank.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department Operations Division Assistant Director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the flash floods were caused by the overflow of the drainage system and not by the phenomenon of unusually high tides.
“Heavy rain this evening caused the drainage system to be overwhelmed by the volume of water, but water levels in the affected areas are now reported to be receding,” he said in a statement yesterday.
Meanwhile, the Selangor Public Works Department (JKR), in a separate statement, said the Jalan Jati Bridge in Section U6, Kampung Melayu Subang, had been closed to all vehicles for safety reasons following severe erosion of the bridge abutment structure.
According to the department, the erosion and embankment collapse occurred following a rise in water levels and strong currents in Sungai Damansara due to continuous heavy rain.
“A Traffic Management Plan has been implemented to regulate vehicle movement, and road users are advised to use the alternative route via Lorong Cempaka and comply with the diversion signs at the location,” the department said.
The department would also carry out temporary repair works in the affected area, subject to site safety conditions and the availability of materials from quarries, as the work would take place during a public holiday period.
For the long term, the department said an allocation would be sought to carry out permanent repairs to the bridge abutment structure and reinforce the banks of Sungai Damansara to ensure the stability of the bridge. — Bernama
* Editor’s note: JKR stands for Jabatan Kerja Raya in Malay.

Title: Flags, ceramah and festive lights: Melaka juggles polls and Deepavali
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 8 — Amid the fervour of the 16th Melaka State Election campaign, filled with political ceramah and party flags, the atmosphere in the historic city centre eased briefly as it was illuminated by Deepavali festivities last night.
A Bernama check at the Stadthuys grounds and Jonker Walk here found that the Melaka Bila Larut Malam programme, November edition: Deepavali 2026, had enlivened the celebration, which continued to flourish undimmed by the current political fervour.
The main stage came alive with cross-cultural performances, featuring lively songs and classical melodies by artistes of various races, alongside nimble dancers in colourful saris and kurtas, including a captivating performance by Badan Warisan Seni Melaka.
The Deepavali festivities also spilled over into the popular Little India Melaka area, which remained crowded with people shopping for last-minute essentials, including new clothes, home decorations and an assortment of traditional sweets and snacks such as
muruku
and
ladoo
.
The business lane resembled a living mural, with rows of shops displaying colourful attire and fresh flower garlands, while henna-painting stalls were filled with women having traditional floral patterns applied to their fingers to complete their look for Deepavali morning.
People of various local communities and foreign tourists also took the opportunity to experience the traditions by wearing traditional attire and enjoying popular street food such as
pani puri
and
samosas
at stalls operating until late at night.
Members of the Indian community shop for last-minute Deepavali essentials at Little India in Melaka City on November 7, 2026. — Bernama pic
Last night’s festivities showed that seasons and political differences should not divide people; instead, Melaka’s cultural diversity and bonds of fellowship remain the foundation of strong unity across all arenas of competition.
The Election Commission has set Nov 14 as polling day for the Melaka state election, with early voting on Nov 10.
More news on the 16th Melaka State Election at https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026. — Bernama

Title: Dashcam footage? Police seek witnesses after couple from Cheras die in North-South Highway skid
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 8 — An elderly couple died after the car they were travelling in skidded into a drain at KM242 of the southbound North-South Expressway (PLUS) here this afternoon.
Rembau District Police Chief Supt Ngiam Ooi Ming said the 75-year-old man was pronounced dead at the scene, while his 70-year-old wife died while receiving treatment at Tuanku Ja’afar Hospital at about 8 pm.
“Preliminary investigations found that the Proton Saga carrying the couple was driven by a 20-year-old man, with another passenger, a 21-year-old woman.
“They were travelling from Cheras, Kuala Lumpur, to Port Dickson.
“On reaching the scene, a group of motorcyclists riding in convoy are believed to have overtaken and suddenly moved into the car’s path, causing it to lose control and skid into a drain on the left side of the highway,” he said in a statement tonight.
Without disclosing the victims’ names in the statement, he said the female passenger was seriously injured and receiving treatment at Rembau Hospital, while the driver was unhurt.
Police are investigating the case under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and would trace the group of motorcyclists believed to have been at the scene.
He also urged members of the public who witnessed the incident or have dashcam footage to contact the Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Division at the Rembau District Police Headquarters to assist with the investigation. — Bernama

Title: Eat, mingle, celebrate: Five Deepavali open houses from Brickfields to Ipoh for all Malaysians
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 8 — If colours make up one half of Deepavali, food makes up the other.  Wolfing down the customary mutton curry and biriyani rice and munching away on murukku is an annual Deepavali ritual for most Malaysian Indian households.
But there is also one truly Malaysian tradition to fete every major festival here — the open house.
An open house is not just an elaborate feast. It is a celebration of family ties, enduring friendships, and an occasion to build new ones.
This year, most public open houses will be held almost a week after Deepavali, giving families time to celebrate at home before sharing the festival with the wider community.
So, for those looking to experience Deepavali in a truly Malaysian way, here are five open houses to visit:
1. National Deepavali Celebration, Brickfields — November 14
One of the biggest open houses will be the National Deepavali Celebration, organised by the National Unity Ministry in the Little India enclave of Brickfields on November 14.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is expected to officiate the day-long event, which will feature arts, cultural performances and exhibitions.
More than 10,000 people are expected to throng the open house that is slated to begin at 8am.
2. Selangor Deepavali Open House, Klang — November 14
On the same day, Selangor will host its state-level Deepavali celebration at 6pm in Dataran Klang @ Padang Chetty in Klang, which is also open to all members of the public.
Some 10,000 visitors are expected to attend and take part in the cultural activities and celebrations.
3. Perak Deepavali Open House, Ipoh — November 14
Outside the Klang Valley, the Perak state government will host an open house starting from 2pm, also on November 14, at Stadium Indera Mulia in Ipoh.
The event will be graced by Perak ruler Sultan Nazrin Shah.
Some 20,000 people are expected to turn up for the celebration, which will feature traditional performances.
4. Johore Bar Deepavali Open House, Muar — November 17
The legal fraternity is also enlivening the celebrations with open houses lined up in the central and south regions.
The Johore Bar will host a Deepavali open house featuring Indian cuisines including tandoori chicken and mutton varuval.
The event will be held at noon on November 17 at the Muar Bar Room.
5. Kuala Lumpur Bar Deepavali Open House, Kuala Lumpur — November 20
The Kuala Lumpur Bar will hold its Deepavali open house at 7pm on November 20 at the KL Bar Auditorium.
The event is open to all but limited to 150 participants on a first-come, first-served basis.

Title: More than new clothes and sweets, Deepavali is about family and tradition
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 7 — Deepavali celebrations are not just about wearing new attire and preparing an array of traditional delicacies, but also about strengthening family bonds and preserving age-old traditions passed down through generations.
For Singaporean P. Parvathy, 65, from Sengkang, a visit to Johor Bahru to shop for Deepavali essentials has become an annual tradition, while also giving her the opportunity to meet relatives living in the state.
She said her visit to the Deepavali Bazaar at Jalan Ungku Puan here also allowed her to browse a variety of decorative items for the home, including floral ornaments to hang at the entrance, traditional attire and bangles.
“I came to buy flowers to hang at the door. After this, I also want to buy clothes and bangles. This year, I find that the items on sale are even more beautiful than before,” she told Bernama recently.
Sharing how Deepavali is celebrated in Singapore, Parvathy said preparations at her home begin on the eve of the festival, with various delicacies prepared to be enjoyed with family members and guests.
She said that on Deepavali morning, the entire family would wake up as early as 5am to bathe, perform prayers and enjoy a traditional breakfast such as thosai before welcoming visits from relatives and friends.
She said the practice of gathering and sharing meals remained one of the traditions that continued to add to the festive atmosphere of her family’s Deepavali celebrations each year.
Little India in Brickfields bustles with activity as shoppers make a last-minute dash for Deepavali essentials. — Bernama pic
Meanwhile, for housewife K. Kalaivani, 40, from Pasir Gudang, this year’s Deepavali holds special significance as her family will also be holding a religious ceremony to mark her daughter’s coming of age.
The mother of four said that apart from preparing traditional attire, including saris, for her family members, she had also bought flowers for the religious ceremony and several other necessities.
She said the preparations were not only for the Deepavali celebrations but also to mark a meaningful occasion for her family in conjunction with her daughter’s religious ceremony.
Meanwhile, traditional snack seller Renuka, 34, who wished to be identified only by her first name, is offering more than 50 varieties of biscuits and savoury snacks in conjunction with Deepavali, giving the Indian community a wide selection to complete their festive spread.
She said sales, which began more than 15 days before Deepavali, allowed customers to choose from a variety of snacks to serve to family members, relatives and guests visiting their homes.
Among the items available are tarts, suji and murukku, priced from RM35 per jar, while customers can purchase four jars at a promotional price of RM120.
She said the variety of snacks also complemented the tradition of visiting family and friends, which adds to the festive atmosphere of Deepavali celebrations each year.
Deepavali, also known as the Festival of Lights, will be celebrated tomorrow by Hindus across the country. — Bernama

Title: This Deepavali, Anwar calls on Malaysians to celebrate differences and shared values
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The Deepavali celebration should serve as a platform to strengthen unity, bridge gaps between communities and foster values of compassion and concern for those in need.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said that in a multiracial society rooted in diverse cultures and traditions, the values of mutual respect, understanding and the acceptance of differences must continue to be reinforced.
“May this Deepavali inspire a renewed spirit to foster a more open, noble and progressive mindset, thereby elevating the dignity of the people and strengthening the nation’s harmony,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Anwar also extended his Deepavali greetings to all those celebrating the festival, expressing his hope that it brings happiness, peace and prosperity.
“Deepavali arrives bearing a ray of joy, enlivening the spirit of the ‘Festival of Lights’, which symbolises the triumph of light over darkness, the victory of goodness over evil, and the power of knowledge to liberate humanity from the shackles of ignorance and arrogance.
“
Deepavali Nalvaalthukkal
! (Deepavali greetings),” he added. — Bernama

Title: After deadly Paya Terubong landslide, Chow says DOSH must finish probe first
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang state government will decide whether to set up a State Commission of Inquiry (SCI) into the Taman Seri Rambai landslide in Paya Terubong once the state Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) completes its investigation and submits its findings and recommendations.
Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would await the findings of the DOSH investigation before considering further action over the incident, which claimed the life of a 73-year-old doctor.
He said he had yet to receive any updates on the progress of the investigation.
“DOSH is conducting its investigation and will provide recommendations (to the state government) once it is completed. A decision on whether to establish an SCI will only be made after that,” he told reporters after officiating at the Penang AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 at SEGi College Penang here today.
He was responding to calls from several quarters for the state government to establish an SCI to conduct an independent investigation into the Oct 25 landslide tragedy.
When asked whether residents affected by the landslide could return to their homes, Chow said the matter had yet to be determined as the area had not been declared safe.
Earlier, several state assemblymen and non-governmental organisations (NGOs) had called for an independent investigation into the fatal landslide and demanded action against those responsible for the hillside development.
In the 8.36 am incident, Dr Wong Kar Lin was killed after being buried in a landslide that struck his home, while his wife, Chang Mei Nuo, 68, and mother-in-law, Wong Poh Lim, who is in her 80s, managed to escape. — Bernama

Title: Zahid says Malaysia stands ready to help Lebanon rebuild after conflict
Article:
ISTANBUL, Nov 7 — Malaysia is ready to help Lebanon rebuild following the conflict that has affected the country, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said this could include rebuilding infrastructure and local economies, providing humanitarian assistance, offering Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), and strengthening defence cooperation to enhance Lebanon’s capabilities and resilience.
“Malaysia and Lebanon share a special friendship, particularly through Malaysia’s involvement in peacekeeping operations under the Malaysian Battalion (MALBATT) since 2007.
“For nearly two decades, our peacekeepers have played an important role in supporting peace and stability in southern Lebanon,” he said here today.
Ahmad Zahid, who is currently in Turkiye for a four-day working visit from Nov 5 to 8 in conjunction with his participation in the TRT World Forum 2026, said he believed Malaysia’s commitment to Lebanon would continue beyond the end of the MALBATT peacekeeping mission in January 2027, following the termination of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (UNIFIL) mandate at the end of this year.
He said the friendship between the two countries should instead continue through cooperation to help Lebanese rebuild their lives, regain hope for the future and achieve lasting peace.
“Peace is not simply the end of war, but the beginning of efforts to rebuild lives,” he said.
Ahmad Zahid, who also serves as Rural and Regional Development Minister, earlier met with Lebanese Deputy Prime Minister Dr Tarek Mitri after the TRT World Forum 2026 at the Istanbul Congress Centre (ICC) yesterday.
Ahmad Zahid also met Developing Eight (D-8) Secretary-General Sohail Mahmood to exchange views on ways to enhance cooperation among member states, particularly in tackling economic challenges and global geopolitical uncertainties.
He said the talks also explored the potential of a market comprising more than 1.2 billion people, noting that D-8 had considerable scope to expand trade, investment and strategic ties among member states.
“I also highlighted opportunities for cooperation in the halal industry, TVET, food security and the development of small and medium enterprises, including expanding economic opportunities for rural communities.
“I believe the strength of D-8 lies not merely in the size of its market, but in its member countries’ ability to translate cooperation into shared prosperity. Malaysia will remain committed to playing an active role in ensuring that this potential is harnessed for the benefit of its people. Insya-Allah,” he said.
Established in 1997, D-8 aims to promote economic cooperation among eight developing countries: Malaysia, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Pakistan, Iran, Turkiye, Egypt and Nigeria.
Ahmad Zahid said both meetings reflected Malaysia’s commitment to active and constructive international engagement, with continued emphasis on dialogue, mutual understanding and practical cooperation in support of peace and shared prosperity. — Bernama

Title: Penang sets aside RM4.5m to grow startups, AI adoption and digital economy
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 7 — The Penang government has allocated RM4.5 million in its 2027 budget to support technology startups, accelerate digitalisation among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) and expand the use of artificial intelligence (AI) across the state’s economy.
Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the allocation is to strengthen the state’s technology start-up ecosystem and help businesses embrace digital transformation.
“In (the state’s) Budget 2027, the state government has set aside RM4.5 million for Digital Penang; it will support technology start-ups, help small and medium enterprises go digital, and use AI across our economy. The startup community supported by the initiative has already generated 310 companies and created approximately 1,720 jobs,” he said when officiating the AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 at SEGi College Penang here today.
Also present at the AI Future Makers Bootcamp 2026 were chairman Lukas J.Tan and SEGi College Penang head of student experience Vincent Tung Chin Aun.
Chow said the collaboration between young innovators and experienced industry players demonstrated the importance of learning across generations as Penang prepared its workforce for technological changes. He noted that the state had successfully adapted to previous industrial transformations, including when the country’s first Free Trade Zone was established in Bayan Lepas in 1972, with workers acquiring new skills through on-the-job training and knowledge-sharing.
“Penang knows how to do this. When the world changed, we learned fast, and we learned together. The world is changing again,” he added, noting that AI could now complete in an afternoon tasks that previously took a week.
On talent development, Chow said 675 fresh graduates and working professionals had undergone chip design training through the Penang Chip Design Academy, with 85 per cent of them securing employment. He said the Penang Talent Focus Group, launched in June under the Penang Workplace initiative, also brought together industry players, universities and human resource practitioners to improve the matching of talent with employment opportunities.
Meanwhile, the Penang Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics (STEM) Blueprint will also introduce AI learning programmes to rural schools through mobile initiatives.
The chief minister urged employers and human resource practitioners to give young job seekers opportunities beyond conventional qualifications, including through interviews, mentoring and professional engagement.
He also encouraged bootcamp participants to turn their ideas into practical solutions and build their innovations in Penang. — Bernama

Title: Najib’s lawyers seek immediate transfer home, say King’s decree must be executed today
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Lawyers for Datuk Seri Najib Razak are contesting the Attorney General’s Chambers’ (AGC) decision to temporarily suspend his house arrest, demanding the former prime minister be transferred to his home immediately.
In a media statement today, the legal firm Messrs Shafee & Co. argued that the AGC’s “temporary suspension” of the house arrest order contradicts the King’s explicit decree issued this morning.
“His Majesty has now spoken. The AGC can honour that commitment in only one way: by allowing the
Titah
(decree) to be carried out today,” the statement read.
The legal team argued that the High Court’s “Order of Discharge on Payment of Fine” issued on November 6 cannot be used to extend Najib’s imprisonment, citing the order’s own recital that the fine has been paid.
“In law, payment of a fine discharges the liability to pay that fine. It cannot, by itself, bring a sentence of imprisonment to an end,” the statement said.
They further asserted that the Pardon is an exercise of the King’s prerogative under Article 42 of the Federal Constitution and is not subject to review by any court or the Attorney General.
The statement noted that the AGC issued a subsequent media statement 57 minutes after the King’s decree, which did not reference the royal order.
According to the legal team, Najib remains in Kajang Prison as of the statement’s issuance, with no effect yet given to the King’s decree.
They have requested the Commissioner General of Prisons to transfer Najib to his residence at No. 11, Jalan Langgak Duta, Taman Duta, Kuala Lumpur.
“His Majesty’s order must be carried out today,” the statement read.

Title: Nancy wants 42,000 men to seek health support and join family decisions
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development (KPWKM) is targeting 42,000 men to benefit from government-provided well-being services for men, as part of efforts to raise awareness of the importance of healthcare among them.
Women, Family and Community Development Minister Datuk Seri Nancy Shukri said the initiative also encouraged men to seek relevant health information and services with their partners, particularly when making decisions about family health.
“I urge men to seek relevant information and services together with their partners when making decisions about family health,” she said at the Selangor International Trade Centre (SITC) here today.
She was speaking at the November National Family Month 2026 celebration, which was launched by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and attended by his wife, Bandar Tun Razak MP Datuk Seri Dr Wan Azizah Wan Ismail, Deputy Women, Family and Community Development Minister Lim Hui Ying, and Selangor State Executive Councillor for Women and Community Welfare Anfaal Saari.
Nancy said the government had allocated RM4.355 billion to KPWKM under Budget 2027, an increase of RM168 million from the previous year.
Of this amount, almost RM3.3 billion was allocated for welfare assistance to strengthen the social safety net and the well-being of those in need.
She said couples facing fertility challenges could also benefit from the Fertility Treatment Assistance and Infertility Advocacy Programme (BuAI), run by the National Population and Family Development Board (LPPKN), which aims to help 2,000 eligible couples receive treatment assistance.
In 2025, a total of 82,679 individuals benefited from the programme, while 1,658 Intrauterine Insemination (IUI) treatment cycles were carried out, resulting in 184 recorded pregnancies.
She said the achievement demonstrated the importance of early detection of fertility problems and access to treatment by qualified specialists. — Bernama

Title: All eyes on Nov 14 as police strengthen readiness for Melaka vote
Article:
MELAKA, Nov 7 — The Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) is strengthening its level of preparedness to ensure public safety and order are maintained throughout the 16th Melaka State Election, which will be held on Nov 14.
According to a post on the Melaka Police Facebook page, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail, in his address during a working visit to the Melaka Contingent Police Headquarters (IPK) yesterday, touched on several matters, including duty assignment, security management and the responsibilities of every personnel in ensuring the smooth conduct of the election process.
“He emphasised that all members of the force must always maintain professionalism, integrity and discipline while carrying out their duties, and ensure that all actions are guided by the law and established standard operating procedures (SOPs),” it added.
According to the post, Mohd Khalid also reminded PDRM personnel to safeguard the confidentiality of official information, strengthen esprit de corps and ensure compliance with the chain of command and control to guarantee the effectiveness of every assignment.
In the same address, he also emphasised the importance of the welfare, safety and physical and mental health of all personnel.
“Supervising officers are also reminded to always pay attention to the needs and welfare of personnel under their supervision, ensuring that their motivation and commitment to carrying out their duties remain at the highest level,” it added.
During the visit, Mohd Khalid also inspected the Melaka State Election Operations Room to gain an overview of operational preparations and the mechanisms for coordinating personnel deployment, and was briefed on the current security situation, local issues, and the contingent’s strategic planning.
“He (Mohd Khalid) also emphasised that the success of the assignments for the 16th Melaka State Election depends on the unity, discipline and preparedness of all PDRM personnel in ensuring that the election is conducted in a peaceful and controlled environment,” it added.
Mohd Khalid subsequently continued his visit to the Melaka Tengah District Police Headquarters (IPD), where he addressed the personnel, urging them to remain prepared, strengthen cooperation and give their full commitment in carrying out their entrusted responsibilities.
Polling is on Nov 14, with early voting set for Nov 10.
For updates on the state election, visit https://election.bernama.com/prn/melaka/2026/. — Bernama

Title: Saifuddin Nasution wants schools, police and health authorities to share data on at-risk students
Article:
KULIM, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), the Ministry of Education (MOE), and the Ministry of Health (MOH) must strengthen their cooperation and information-sharing to address various security issues and create a safe school ecosystem.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said these three ministries cannot work in isolation when dealing with the various issues that arise within schools.
He noted that this necessity was among the matters discussed during a meeting of the Police-Ministry of Education Consultative Committee, held last week at the Police Training Centre (Pulapol).
“One of the points I raised concerns student profiling. For instance, there are students who require treatment and consultation with a psychiatrist, yet the school authorities lack access to such information, which is held by the Ministry of Health,” he said.
He made these remarks to reporters after attending the ‘Semarak Kebudayaan Masyarakat Kedah Bersama PDRM 2026’ programme here today.
He was asked to comment on media reports regarding the police’s arrest of two teenagers believed to be suppliers in a case involving a school student in Negeri Sembilan who vaped using an electronic cigarette containing drugs.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan was reported as saying that the arrested suspects include a 17-year-old student (a schoolmate of the victim) and an 18-year-old male who is no longer in school.
Saifuddin Nasution emphasised that collaboration among the three ministries is crucial, given that the school security ecosystem encompasses approximately 5.2 million students across 12,000 schools nationwide, a situation that necessitates information-sharing and integrated action among the relevant agencies.
Meanwhile, he noted that the use of vapes among students has also become a point of concern, as the contents of vape liquids — which may include a variety of substances — can complicate police investigations.
He explained that some substances may contain toxic components that have not yet been officially classified as poisons; this creates challenges for the police in completing investigations and bringing cases to the prosecution stage.
He said existing collaboration between the police and schools which includes the deployment of police liaison officers and the involvement of the National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) needs to be expanded to also include the Ministry of Health (MOH).
“The issue is not limited to vape use among students; it also encompasses various other activities, such as bullying and accidents occurring within school premises,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Two step-sisters killed after car skids and crashes on PLUS highway near Tanjong Malim
Article:
IPOH, Nov 7 — Two step-siblings died when the vehicle they were in skidded in an accident at Kilometre 388 of the North-South Expressway (Plus) southbound, near Tanjong Malim today.
Muallim district police chief Supt Khalid Mohamad said an 18-year-old girl was pronounced dead at the scene, while a six-year-old girl who suffered severe injuries died while receiving treatment at the Slim River Hospital.
He said the driver, a 27-year-old man, and another female passenger, aged 20, sustained injuries and were taken to the same hospital for further treatment.
“In the incident at about 8.30am, a vehicle travelling from Perlis towards Kuala Lumpur is believed to have lost control before veering off to the left shoulder of the road and crashing into the road barrier,” he said in a statement today.
Khalid said the case was classified under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987 and further investigations are being conducted to identify the actual cause of the accident.
He urged witnesses to the accident to contact the investigating officer, Inspector Muhammad Taufiq Abd Aziz, at 016-4184507 to assist with the investigation.
Earlier, Perak Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said a team from the Tanjong Malim Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene after receiving a call regarding the accident at 8.35am. — Bernama

Title: Fahmi says online banking remains safe despite cyberattacks and Bank Rakyat hack
Article:
DOHA, Nov 7 — The country’s online banking system and financial transactions remain secure despite attempted cyberattacks by non-state actors, including a recent hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Communications Minister and Madani government spokesperson Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said.
He said the hacking attempts detected so far had not resulted in data theft or affected the country’s online banking operations.
“We have identified attempts by non-state actors to launch cyberattacks, including hacking, but so far there has been no data theft or disruption to online banking systems.
“So, our banking and financial sectors remain secure, and online transactions are safe,” he said when asked by a Malaysian about the latest cyberattacks targeting the country, particularly the hacking of Bank Rakyat’s website, after attending the bowling event at the 2026 Malaysian Games in Qatar (Suqma 2026) here today.
Malaysia’s Ambassador to Qatar Faizal Razali and Malaysian Association of Qatar (MAQ) president Dr Mohd Faris Khamidi were also present.
On the hacking incident involving Bank Rakyat’s website, Fahmi said it was confined to changes to the website’s appearance and involved a third-party-managed site.
“In the latest development, Bank Rakyat reported that its third-party-managed website had been hacked, but the incident was limited to web defacement and the website had been taken over,” he said.
He said Bank Rakyat had blocked access to the affected server and redirected users to the i-Rakyat website, which the bank fully owns.
Meanwhile, Fahmi said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had ordered the National Security Council (MKN) to review potential security threats to various national infrastructure facilities, particularly hybrid threats, as early as the beginning of last week.
He said the exercise involved examining internet infrastructure, websites and databases to ensure continued protection of the country’s digital assets.
“At yesterday’s Cabinet meeting, the Prime Minister called for a more thorough review of cybersecurity across all government assets, banking institutions and government-linked companies, including by the National Cyber Security Agency and the MKN,” he said.
Fahmi is leading the Malaysian delegation to the 2026 International Telecommunication Union Plenipotentiary Conference (ITU PP-26), from Nov 6 to 11, an important platform for the country’s participation in international discussions and cooperation on telecommunications and digital technology.
His working visit to Doha also includes efforts to retain Malaysia’s seat on the ITU Council for the 2027-2030 term. — Bernama

Title: Flood evacuees in Selangor, Perak nearly triple to over 4,000 in hours
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The flood situation in Selangor and Perak continued to worsen, with the number of evacuees at temporary relief centres (PPS) rising to 4,068 this afternoon from 1,404 this morning.
In
SELANGOR
, the number of flood evacuees still sheltering at PPS this afternoon rose to 3,798 from 128 families at two centres, compared with 1,206 from 316 families at nine centres this morning.
According to the Social Welfare Department’s (JKM) InfoBencana portal, PPS Sekolah Agama Batu Lapan Ijok is sheltering 2,999 evacuees from 67 families, while 799 evacuees from 61 families are at Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Mahang.
Meanwhile, in
PERAK
, the number of flood and storm evacuees rose to 270 from 79 families this afternoon, compared with 198 from 58 families this morning, across the Hilir Perak and Manjung districts.
The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat (JBPN) said in a statement that the number of evacuees at PPS Dewan Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan (MPTI) Langkap remained at 137 from 40 victims, while the number at PPS Dewan Rumah Rehat MPTI rose to 107 from 32 families.
Meanwhile, 26 people from seven families affected by the storm are still sheltering at PPS Dewan Komuniti Manjung.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast rain in all districts tonight. — Bernama

Title: AG seeks audience with King to clarify Najib’s house arrest issue, says Anwar
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 7 — Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar has requested an audience with His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, to discuss former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest in his SRC International case, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today.
Anwar stressed that the Agong’s power to grant pardons was not being disputed, but said there was a legal issue involving Najib’s 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case that required clarification by the courts.
“I have asked for the Attorney General to immediately meet the Agong to ‘
mohon ampun
’ (apologise) and explain why that decision was accepted for the SRC case, but there is a problem as it involves the second case, which is the 1MDB case.
“So to explain and maybe we need a few days to decide after referring to the judiciary. I also only leave it to the Attorney General to elaborate on this case, because this is not the prime minister’s jurisdiction,” he told reporters after launching the National Family Month celebrations at the Selangor International Trade Centre (SITC) here.
Anwar later added that the AG had already requested an audience with the King to explain the house arrest issue.
Earlier, Anwar said he wanted to avoid this house arrest matter from becoming politicised.
“But I want to explain that the Yang di-Pertuan Agong’s powers is not disputed, that’s the first, that’s in the SRC case as stated by the Pardons Board.
“The case that arises in the second case, whether it can be carried out or not, that is a decision that will be finalised by the Attorney General and the judiciary, that’s all,” he said, adding that the dissatisfaction by some on the house arrest issue is beyond his jurisdiction.
Anwar had also said preparations had been made to carry out the house arrest in the SRC International case in line with the Agong’s pardon, but said the Attorney General faced constraints as the matter was related to the 1MDB case, and that was why a few days are needed to finalise it.
Separately, the Prime Minister’s Office this evening issued a statement to confirm that the Attorney General had today requested for an audience with His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim to apologise and to express his stand in complying with the King’s decree on the conditional pardon in Najib’s SRC International case.
“The Attorney General will also explain the legal matter that arose from the High Court’s Order of Discharge following the payment of the RM50 million fine, and that has to be decided by the courts as it gives an impact on the date when the jail sentence in the 1MDB case will start,” the brief statement said.
In 2024, a royal pardon over Najib’s SRC International case resulted in the reduction of his 12-year jail term to six years, and his RM210 million fine to RM50 million.
On September 18, Najib was given a conditional pardon in his SRC International case, which allowed him to serve the rest of his jail term under house arrest until August 23, 2028, if he pays the RM50 million fine.
Separately, Najib is facing a 15-year jail term in his 1MDB case, with the High Court in December 2025 ordering the imprisonment to be carried out immediately after the end of his SRC International jail term.
Najib is currently appealing his 1MDB conviction and sentence, and the High Court had on October 14 rejected his bid to stay or to pause the carrying out of the 1MDB sentence.
Umno yesterday paid the RM50 million fine on Najib’s behalf, but he is currently still at Kajang Prison as the Attorney General yesterday highlighted the need to clarify legal matters linked to the house arrest.
Earlier today, Istana Negara issued a statement saying that His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim’s conditional pardon order was clear and unambiguous and unrelated to any other cases against Najib, and said there should not be any confusion over its interpretation or prolonged uncertainty over its implementation.
Istana Negara also said that any dispute of the conditional pardon order would amount to disobeying the King’s order.
Prior to Anwar’s remarks this afternoon, the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) today issued a lengthy statement that explained it was not disputing or setting aside or intended to suspend the Agong’s conditional pardon order for Najib’s house arrest.
The AGC said it was necessary for the court to decide on uncertainties regarding whether the RM50 million fine payment meant the SRC International sentence had been fully resolved or if Najib still had to serve the remaining term on house arrest.

Title: Bukit Aman suspects cocaine-in-shoes arrest at Hong Kong airport linked to Malaysia drug bust
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The arrest of a Hong Kong man with about one kilogramme of cocaine concealed in his shoes at Hong Kong International Airport after arriving from Kuala Lumpur last Wednesday is believed to be linked to an international drug trafficking syndicate recently crippled by the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM).
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the suspected link was based on similarities in the modus operandi, type of drugs and trafficking destinations, namely Hong Kong, Japan and Indonesia.
“We believe the syndicate has been crippled following the arrest of a Hong Kong national believed to be the syndicate leader and a local recruiter, as announced at yesterday’s press conference,” he said when contacted today.
Media reports today said a 36-year-old Hong Kong man was arrested last Wednesday after customs officers found cocaine estimated to be worth HK$600,000 (RM311,000) during an inspection at Hong Kong International Airport following his arrival from Malaysia.
Hussein said PDRM had been informed by Hong Kong authorities of the arrest and drug seizure, adding that both sides had exchanged relevant information.
He said the cocaine did not originate from Malaysia, but the country was believed to have been used as a transit hub before the drugs were smuggled to their intended destinations through Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) or Penang International Airport.
Yesterday, media reports said PDRM had arrested four individuals, including a Hong Kong national believed to be the mastermind of the syndicate, during an operation at a homestay in Brickfields here on Nov 5.
During the operation, police also seized 450 grammes of cocaine and two pairs of shoes believed to have been intended for two individuals recruited as drug mules.
The syndicate, believed to have been active since September, was found to have recruited Malaysians to smuggle drugs overseas.
Those recruited included five individuals arrested by authorities at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport in Jakarta and another five at Haneda International Airport in Tokyo in September and October. — Bernama

Title: Tourism Ministry open to helping international event organisers facing funding challenges, says Tiong
Article:
SIBU, Nov 7 — The Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture (Motac) is prepared to consider collaborating with and providing assistance to organisers of international events in Malaysia, particularly those facing financial constraints.
Minister Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing said the move was aimed at encouraging more international events to be held in the country while attracting greater participation from overseas.
“This is in line with the ministry’s aim to strengthen Malaysia’s presence on the international stage by hosting events that attract participants from various countries,” he told reporters at the International Archery Coaching and Wellness Forum and Workshop 2026 here today.
He said such events could also attract more visitors and serve as a platform for local and international participants to share knowledge, experiences and skills.
“We hope next year’s forum and coaching workshop can be expanded to involve more participating countries,” he said.
Tiong said the ministry would also explore possible forms of collaboration and assistance to help organisers address their financial challenges. — Bernama

Title: DAP yet to discuss replacing Anthony Loke as transport minister, says party vice-chairman
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — DAP has yet to discuss a replacement for Transport Minister Anthony Loke, whose resignation remains conditional on former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak returning home to serve the remainder of his prison sentence under house arrest.
DAP vice-chairman Syahredzan Johan said discussions about a potential successor would be premature because Loke’s resignation had not taken effect, the
New Straits Times
reported.
“For now, his resignation has not taken effect until Datuk Seri Najib sets foot in his house, so it is inappropriate to discuss who the replacement will be,” he said when contacted.
Syahredzan also stressed that Cabinet appointments remained the prerogative of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who would consult DAP’s leadership before making any decision.
“Cabinet appointments are the prerogative of the prime minister. Of course, the prime minister will make a decision after discussions with the DAP secretary-general himself,” he said.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, reaffirmed yesterday that his resignation would take effect only when Najib physically returned home to begin serving his sentence under house arrest.
He had submitted his resignation letter to Anwar on September 28 in protest against the conditional royal pardon granted to Najib, reflecting DAP’s opposition to the house arrest arrangement.
The uncertainty over Loke’s departure follows the payment of Najib’s RM50 million fine yesterday, fulfilling a key condition of the royal pardon.
The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) subsequently sought a temporary deferment of Najib’s transfer to house arrest, citing unresolved legal questions over the effect of the conditional pardon and a court discharge order.
The AGC said clarification was needed on the implications for Najib’s separate 15-year prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case, which is under appeal.
Istana Negara, however, maintained today that the conditional pardon granted by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim was clear and unambiguous, and that all its conditions had been fulfilled.
The AGC has said it is not challenging the King’s constitutional power to grant pardons but is seeking judicial clarification to ensure that the relevant orders are implemented lawfully.
Najib, 73, has been imprisoned since August 2022 following his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million belonging to SRC International, a former subsidiary of 1MDB.
On September 18, Sultan Ibrahim granted Najib a conditional royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and other stipulated conditions.

Title: Teenager, 19, dies after being stabbed during alleged argument at Sibu park
Article:
SIBU, Nov 7 — A 19-year-old youth died after being stabbed in the chest during an incident at a public park along Jalan Gambir here around midnight last night.
The victim was reportedly at the park with a group of young men and women when an argument broke out, allegedly leading to the stabbing.
He sustained a stab wound to the chest and was rushed to hospital for emergency treatment but later succumbed to his injuries.
It is understood that nearby residents heard a woman screaming from the direction of the park, prompting them to alert the police.
Police are believed to have arrested two men in their 20s to assist in investigations.
When contacted today, Sibu District Police Chief ACP Abang Zainal Abidin Abang Ahmad confirmed that the case was still under investigation.
“The case is still under further investigation,” he said. — The Borneo Post

Title: Security presence disappears from Najib’s Taman Duta residence as house arrest remains on hold
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — The security presence outside former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s residence was nowhere to be seen today, a day after the Taman Duta property was placed under tight security ahead of his anticipated return under house arrest.
According to
Astro Awani
, no police officers or Prisons Department vehicles were visible outside the Jalan Langgak Duta residence, while yellow security tape restricting access to the property had also been removed.
The scene contrasted sharply with Friday, when security personnel controlled access to the residence, allowing only authorised individuals and vehicles to enter or leave.
The heightened security came as preparations were made for Najib’s expected return after he paid a RM50 million fine in the SRC International corruption case, fulfilling a key condition of a royal pardon allowing him to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028.
However, the move was put on hold after the Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) called for further legal clarification on the implementation of the conditional pardon.
Despite the absence of security personnel today, local and international journalists remained stationed near the residence, awaiting further developments.
Najib’s residence was officially gazetted as a prison on Friday under Section 3 of the Prisons Act 1995, following a declaration by Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
The designation covers the property and its surrounding land, allowing it to be used for the detention of individuals in lawful custody.
In a statement today, the AGC called for an urgent court determination on whether Najib’s SRC International prison sentence remains in force or has legally ended following the payment of the fine.
It said the distinction was crucial because Najib’s separate 15-year prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) corruption case was ordered to begin after the completion of his SRC International sentence.
The AGC also rejected allegations that it was challenging the authority of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, maintaining that its request for judicial clarification was intended to ensure the royal decree and existing court orders were implemented lawfully.
The clarification came after Istana Negara said the conditional pardon granted to Najib was clear and unambiguous, warning that any attempt to dispute the decree could amount to defying the King’s order.
Najib, 73, has been serving a prison sentence since August 2022 following his conviction for offences involving RM42 million in SRC International funds.
His original 12-year sentence was reduced to six years under a partial royal pardon in 2024, while his RM210 million fine was cut to RM50 million.
A subsequent conditional pardon granted on September 18 this year allowed him to serve the remaining term under house arrest, subject to payment of the fine and compliance with stipulated conditions.

Title: Integrity must go hand in hand with academic success, Perlis Raja Muda tells UniSIRAJ graduates
Article:
KANGAR, Nov 7 — Universiti Islam Antarabangsa Tuanku Syed Sirajuddin (UniSIRAJ) graduates must be trustworthy and uphold integrity, respect differences and stand by the truth - qualities that should guide them as they embark on their careers and future lives.
Raja Muda of Perlis Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra Jamalullail, who is also UniSIRAJ Chancellor, said knowledge developed one’s ability to think and solve problems, while good manners reflected one’s values.
“Ensure that academic excellence and expertise are always accompanied by strong moral values and principles,” he said at the 9th UniSIRAJ Convocation Ceremony at Dewan 2020 here today.
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said that in an era of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital advancement, the pursuit of knowledge must always go hand in hand with noble values and strong principles.
He also said graduates should build their careers diligently, discharge their responsibilities well and leverage their expertise to generate ideas and solutions that would add value to organisations and society.
“Success is not merely about positions, income or personal achievements, but also about the benefits one brings to others. The journey after convocation will not necessarily be easy.
“Failures, competition and changes will test one’s abilities. Turn every challenge into an opportunity to learn, address weaknesses and improve one’s capabilities. Face them with patience, perseverance and faith in Allah, without compromising one’s principles or self-respect,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said knowledge and expertise must translate into actions that bring benefits to others. Those who become leaders should lead with integrity, educators should teach with a strong sense of responsibility, while professionals should carry out their duties conscientiously and prioritise the interests of humanity.
Tuanku Syed Faizuddin Putra said every position and opportunity should be regarded as a platform to serve others.
At the convocation ceremony, the Raja Muda of Perlis also presented the Chancellor’s Award (Martabat Al-Syaraf Al-Ula) to Maryam Al Adzra Mohd Zawawi, a Bachelor of Hadith graduate from the Faculty of Al-Quran and Sunnah, who achieved a cumulative grade point average (CGPA) of 3.95.
A total of 277 UniSIRAJ graduates received their respective Doctor of Philosophy (PhD), Master’s, Bachelor’s and Diploma scrolls at the ceremony. — Bernama

Title: The journey home begins: Deepavali rush brings slow traffic to major highways across Malaysia
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Traffic on several major highways across the country began to slow down this afternoon as vehicle numbers increased, with members of the public starting their journeys ahead of Deepavali tomorrow.
A Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) spokesperson said the affected routes included the northbound stretch of the North-South Expressway (PLUS) E1 from Trolak to Bidor, Gopeng to Simpang Pulai, Alor Pongsu to Jawi, and Perai to Bertam, along with the southbound stretch from Perai to Juru.
In addition, traffic on the North-South Expressway (PLUS) E2 was also building up and moving slowly at several stretches, including the northbound route from Sungai Besi Toll Plaza to the city centre, Bandar Seri Putra to Bangi, Sedenak to Ayer Hitam, and Skudai to Senai, as well as the southbound route from Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) to Bangi, Nilai to Senawang, and Kempas to Pasir Gudang.
“Traffic was also slow at the Johor Causeway, from Woodlands Checkpoint (CIQ) in Singapore to Sultan Iskandar CIQ in Johor in the northbound direction, while congestion was reported on the Second Link Expressway, from the Second Link Bridge to Sultan Abu Bakar CIQ in Johor, also northbound,” they said when contacted today.
Traffic volume had also increased on the North-South Expressway Central Link (ELITE), affecting the northbound stretches from Gamuda Cove to Bandar Saujana Putra and Putra Heights to Shah Alam, as well as the southbound stretch from Putra Heights to Gamuda Cove.
On the Cheras-Kajang Expressway (GrandSaga), traffic was slow on the northbound stretch from Bandar Tun Hussein Onn to Taman Suntex, while on the Kuala Lumpur-Karak Expressway (KLK), the affected routes were from Gombak Toll Plaza to Lentang and from KM78.9 to Karak Toll Plaza in the eastbound direction.
Meanwhile, on the Sungai Besi Expressway (BESRAYA), traffic was slow on the northbound stretches from Bandar Tasik Selatan to Kuchai and Serdang to Pekan Sungai Besi.
On the Damansara-Puchong Expressway (LDP), the affected stretches were Kelana Jaya to Damansara Utama and Bandar Bukit Puchong to Jalan Majlis in the northbound direction, while traffic was slow from Penchala to Damansara Utama and Sunway to Bandar Bukit Puchong in the southbound direction.

Title: Umno leaders lodge police reports, Dr Akmal demands action on Najib’s house arrest delay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 7 — Several Umno leaders in Johor have lodged a police report over the delay in implementing former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s house arrest, as Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Muhammad Akmal Saleh called for similar reports to be filed nationwide.
Pontian Umno chief Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan, who is also a party supreme council member, lodged the report at the Benut police station at 12.30pm today, accompanied by his deputy Mohd Sumali Reduan, division vice-chief Jamaludin Abd Majid and several grassroots leaders.
“A police report was lodged over the delay in implementing the house arrest order for Najib, which should have been carried out,” Ahmad said in a Facebook post.
Meanwhile, Dr Akmal said Umno Youth branches at state and division levels would lodge police reports to seek an investigation into whether any laws had been breached in delaying the implementation of the royal pardon and related court order.
In a statement today, he urged the government to immediately implement the conditional pardon granted by His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, maintaining that all stipulated conditions had been fulfilled.
“On November 6, all conditions were met. The RM50 million fine was paid at the Kuala Lumpur High Court, which then issued a sealed order allowing Datuk Seri Najib to serve the remainder of his sentence under house arrest. The Home Ministry also gazetted his residence as a prison under Section 3 of the Prisons Act 1995,” Akmal said.
He argued that further legal proceedings should not delay the implementation of the order.
“Umno Youth demands that His Majesty’s decree be implemented immediately. Any further court reference should not be used as grounds to stall a decree that His Majesty has confirmed to be clear and unambiguous,” he said.
Pasir Gudang Umno Youth was also expected to lodge a similar police report against the Attorney General at the Seri Alam district police headquarters.
The moves follow the Attorney General’s Chambers’ (AGC) call yesterday for Najib’s house arrest to be temporarily deferred pending clarification of legal questions surrounding his conditional pardon.
The AGC said the questions centred on whether payment of the RM50 million fine meant Najib’s remaining prison sentence in the SRC International case continued under house arrest or was deemed completed.
It said the interpretation could affect when Najib’s separate prison sentence in the 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) case should begin.
In a further statement today, the AGC denied attempting to override the King’s authority, maintaining that judicial clarification was necessary to prevent conflicting interpretations of the court orders and ensure their lawful implementation.
Istana Negara, meanwhile, reaffirmed today that the conditional pardon granted on September 18 was clear and unambiguous, and that all stipulated conditions had been fulfilled.
The pardon allows Najib to serve the remainder of his SRC International sentence under house arrest until August 23, 2028, subject to payment of the RM50 million fine and compliance with other conditions.
Najib has been imprisoned since August 2022 following his conviction over the misappropriation of RM42 million in SRC International funds.
